concepts.name: Greenlight
concepts.one_liner: Commission a human creator from chat. Your USDC waits in Base's audited AuthCaptureEscrow until you approve the final cut, so the agent economy gets pay-on-delivery.
concepts.target_user: PayBox users who need short creative work fast: podcasters, founders, small brands and creators wanting logo stings, title cards, 10-30 s AI-assisted film shots or music cues. On the other side, independent motion designers and AI filmmakers (the Lumara crowd) who want paid work sourced by agents, with payment certainty.
concepts.problem: Agents pay instantly but creative work arrives later. Today the buyer prepays and hopes (stablecoins have no chargebacks, and about 11% of paid x402 endpoints don't deliver what they promise), or the creator works and hopes. x402's auth-capture scheme (v1.1, Aug 2026) and Base's audited AuthCaptureEscrow both exist, but no facilitator supports auth-capture and PayBox only signs exact x402. No agent wallet offers pay-on-delivery. RentAHuman holds funds custodially and takes 18%. PayBox's catalog has zero Creative coverage.
concepts.hero_flow: 1) User in Claude.ai: 'Commission a 10-second animated sting for my podcast Margin Call, gritty crypto satire, $25, due in 2 hours.' 2) Agent: discover_plugins, then use_plugin greenlight_quote {brief, medium:'motion', budget_usdc:25, deadline}. The backend matches its opted-in human roster (portfolio, rate, turnaround, wallet screened with GoPlus address_security) and returns an offer with the exact PaymentInfo: operator = Greenlight operator, payer, receiver = creator, token = USDC, maxAmount 25e6, preApprovalExpiry +10 min, authorizationExpiry deadline+72h, refundExpiry +7d, fee 0. It also returns plain-language terms and the license. The agent calls core get_portfolio; on a shortfall it calls core get_buy_link (MoonPay on-ramp, usdc_base). 3) greenlight_fund {offer_id, payer}. On first use only, this returns an EVM proposal USDC.approve(PreApprovalPaymentCollector, 25e6) [one-time approval]. It then returns an EVM proposal PreApprovalPaymentCollector.preApprove(paymentInfo) [APPROVAL 'Greenlight']. The backend operator detects the pre-approval and calls AuthCaptureEscrow.authorize(paymentInfo, 25e6, collector, ''), which moves 25 USDC into escrow. greenlight_status reads paymentState(hash), returns the Basescan link, and the creator is pinged on Telegram. 4) The creator (the builder, on camera) uploads the MP4 on the Greenlight creator page and signs an EIP-712 license covering the deliverable SHA-256, the buyer and the rights. The backend runs objective checks: format, 10 s +/-0.5, 1080p, delivered before the deadline. 5) greenlight_status returns a watermarked preview, the check results and the license. User: 'Approve the final cut.' greenlight_release returns an EVM proposal FinalCut.release(paymentInfoHash) [APPROVAL 'Final cut']. The backend sees Released(hash, sender == payer) and calls AuthCaptureEscrow.capture(paymentInfo, 25e6, 0, 0x0). The creator receives 25 USDC, and the buyer gets the full-res file plus a signed license receipt (deliverable hash + capture tx). 6) Unhappy paths: if the deadline is missed, the operator calls void() and the USDC returns to the payer. A buyer dispute calls FinalCut.dispute(hash), which freezes auto-capture. If the operator disappears, greenlight_reclaim returns AuthCaptureEscrow.reclaim(paymentInfo), which only the payer can call, after authorizationExpiry.
concepts.wow_moment: Split screen. The buyer taps 'Approve final cut' in Claude, and the creator's phone buzzes as 25 USDC arrives from an audited escrow on Base. Basescan shows authorize then capture, and the sting plays full-res. Then a missed-deadline commission voids and the money goes home. VO: 'An AI hired me, and neither of us had to trust the other.'
concepts.novel_mechanism: Pay-on-delivery for agent commerce: x402 auth-capture semantics reached through plain PayBox EVM proposals. preApprove is the funding approval, and a backend operator then authorizes into Base's audited AuthCaptureEscrow. Capture fires only on the payer's on-chain 'final cut' consent event, from an event-only FinalCut contract that holds no funds or allowances. Payer-only reclaim is the trustless exit, and the license receipt binds the deliverable hash, the creator's EIP-712 signature and the capture tx. The operator cannot redirect money: capture can only pay the PaymentInfo receiver, and void can only return funds to the payer.

concepts.backend_and_contracts: Hono API on Railway with Postgres (roster, commissions, PaymentInfo) and R2 for deliverables. viem watchers follow the collector pre-approval and FinalCut events. An operator EOA (Railway secret, about $5 of ETH on Base) calls AuthCaptureEscrow v1.1.0 at 0xf96815976523E00e65Be8f34cA5e64b4f41EB19c (authorize, capture, void). Hashes come from escrow.getHash() so encoding can't drift, and every path gets Foundry fork tests against Base mainnet. The one new contract is FinalCut.sol: about 30 lines, event-only release/dispute keyed by paymentInfoHash, holding no funds and no allowances. Other contracts: USDC 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, plus PreApprovalPaymentCollector and OperatorRefundCollector from the base/commerce-payments deployments. A creator web app (Next.js + wagmi) handles profile, rates, upload and EIP-712 license signing, with notifications from a Telegram bot. The bundle holds 6 stable tools that only call the backend and Alchemy. Matching, checks and auto-capture windows live in the backend and can keep evolving after the upload lock.
concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability: Buyer USDC (the builder's PayBox wallet) goes into the audited AuthCaptureEscrow. On capture it goes to the creator wallet (the builder's second wallet or a friend); on void or reclaim it goes back to the buyer. Demo money is 100% recoverable apart from Base gas (cents). The fee is 0 for the hackathon; later, a min/max fee in basis points to the builder's feeReceiver is the business model. Spend: FinalCut deploy under $1, an operator gas buffer of about $5 (recoverable), hosting about $10. Two $25 test cycles fit easily in $100.
concepts.compliance: Non-custodial: funds sit only in an audited escrow. The operator can capture only to the named creator or void to the payer, and the payer can always reclaim after expiry. The builder never holds user funds. Every money move is a PayBox-approved plugin proposal, with no off-chain signature relays and no credential pass-through. Creator and buyer wallets are screened with GoPlus. Content rules ban real-person likeness without consent and IP infringement; creators attest originality, and the license terms are explicit. Framed as escrowed commissions, not insurance. No regulated product, so geofencing beyond sanctions screening isn't needed. No Lumara, MoonPay or Base endorsement claims. Design decisions are documented in the repo, and the demo shows the builder's own human-made work.
concepts.differentiation: First-party plugins (world, aave, kamino, jupiter, hyperliquid, sunrise) are all DeFi/trading. Curated x402 has no creative services, and creative x402 sellers (StableStudio, Gondola) sell AI-only generation with no delivery guarantee. Launch partners (AgentRes, Purch, BRIJ) are bookings and shopping. RentAHuman is custodial with an 18% fee and an X-API-Key. Fiverr and Upwork aren't agent-payable. No x402 facilitator supports auth-capture, and Coinbase Agentic Wallets and Crossmint have no escrowed commissions. Greenlight runs agent to human, so it is not on the A2A kill list, and it is the first pay-on-delivery flow inside an agent wallet.
key_risks: PaymentInfo encoding or hash bugs, or a wrong collector address, could leave funds stuck until reclaim
Two-sided cold start: creator supply
First-time flow needs 3 approvals (allowance, fund, release)
Subjective disputes after delivery
Operator hot-key compromise or downtime
PayBox window shows raw calldata, so escrow semantics are invisible there
Content, IP or likeness abuse
concepts.mitigations: Compute hashes with escrow.getHash() and test every path on a Base fork, then with $1 live. authorizationExpiry plus payer-only reclaim means funds can never be permanently stuck. Seed the roster with the builder and 3-5 invited motion designers, with Lumara outreach after judging. Size the allowance step to the budget and label it as one-time setup. Dispute policy: objective checks, a 48 h review window, then auto-capture. A missed deadline auto-voids, and reclaim is always available. The operator key has bounded power (it cannot redirect funds), minimal ETH, and an alert-and-pause switch. Every tool returns an exact plain-language summary, and on-chain state is re-read after each tx. A content policy plus creator attestation stands behind each license receipt.
concepts.demo_script: 0:00-0:06 Builder at his edit bay; phone buzzes 'New commission $25, due 18:00'. Own-voice VO: 'An AI just hired me, and neither of us has to trust the other.' 0:06-0:16 Claude.ai: the brief, then the Greenlight offer card (creator, $25, deadline, license, escrow terms). 0:16-0:24 PayBox window, Face ID passkey on 'Greenlight'. Basescan: authorize, 25 USDC held in AuthCaptureEscrow. 0:24-0:40 Time-lapse of the builder animating the sting in real software, upload, checks pass. 0:40-0:52 Watermarked preview plays in Claude; 'Approve the final cut'; passkey. 0:52-1:02 Split screen: creator phone shows +25 USDC, Basescan capture tx, signed license receipt in chat. 1:02-1:12 Unhappy path: a second commission misses its deadline, voids, and USDC returns to the buyer on Basescan. 1:12-1:22 The finished sting plays full-screen. End card: 'Greenlight: pay-on-delivery for agents, live in PayBox', with tx hashes.
concepts.why_it_wins_first: Among finalists, 1st usually goes to originality plus a visible real-world outcome. Greenlight is the only concept that ships a new economic primitive into a consumer agent wallet: pay-on-delivery escrow on audited contracts, while auth-capture still has no facilitator. Its outcome is human (a real artist paid on camera). It fills the empty Creative track with something more than an AI wrapper, and it turns PayBox's approval rule into the two natural consent points of a commission. It also plays to the builder's rarest edge: he is the creator in the film, which settles the 'visibly human-made' gate. Next-day GTM for MoonPay: 'Commission an AI filmmaker from Claude, pay on delivery', pitched (with consent) to Lumara's 700+ entrants ahead of the Oct 26 NYC awards. It also gives MoonPay, as an x402 Foundation Premier member, a live auth-capture story. My top pick for 1st.

concepts.name: Aisle
concepts.one_liner: Buy from any MoonPay Commerce merchant in one tap, from a link or a tweet. Merchants are verified, receipts are on-chain, and stablecoin purchases can be returned for the first time.
concepts.target_user: PayBox users buying digital goods and services from independent MoonPay Commerce merchants (creators, indie software, communities). On the other side, the 6,000+ Commerce merchants, many of them Coinbase Commerce refugees, who want agent sales and a way to handle agent returns from chat.
concepts.problem: MoonPay Commerce says every merchant is 'already agent-payable' via POST api.hel.io/v1/x402/checkout/{paylinkId}, but in practice it doesn't work yet. Standard x402 clients, PayBox's generic path included, omit the mandatory payerAddress. Agents can't discover Commerce merchants or tell a real paylink from a phishing one. Paylinks with required customer fields fail with X402_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURES. Nothing confirms the merchant actually got paid through the 30-120 s sweep. And a stablecoin purchase can't be returned, which is the top objection from merchants and shoppers, sharpened by the October 2026 rogue-agent news.
concepts.hero_flow: 1) Buyer in Claude.ai pastes an X post from @shop ('Dusk LUT pack, $9, agent-payable') and says 'Buy this with my Base USDC.' 2) use_plugin aisle_inspect {link}. The backend reads the post (X syndication) and extracts the moonpay.hel.io paylink. It GETs api.hel.io/v1/paylink/{id}/public and fetches the merchant manifest at shop.example/.well-known/agent-commerce.json (paylink ids, @handle, return policy). It decodes the live 402 PAYMENT-REQUIRED (USDC, eip155:8453, 9000000) and screens payTo with GoPlus. Result: 'Verified shop.example, @shop and paylink; 9.00 USDC; 7-day returns.' 3) Core get_portfolio. On a shortfall, Aisle returns needs_funding and the agent calls core get_buy_link (MoonPay on-ramp). 4) aisle_buy {paylink_id, payer_address from list_credentials, chain} returns an x402 proposal: POST https://api.hel.io/v1/x402/checkout/{id}?payerAddress=0x... (empty JSON), maxAmount 9000000, expiry 4 min. PayBox re-fetches and verifies the 402 [APPROVAL 1: passkey], then signs EIP-3009 and Helio settles. 5) Agent polls get_request and passes the paid response to aisle_receipt. The plugin reads the Base USDC Transfer (Alchemy) and polls Helio until the sweep lands, then returns a receipt (merchant, item, amount, tx, 'merchant received') plus a journal line. The merchant's phone shows the MoonPay Commerce 'New payment $9.00'. 6) Buyer: 'Wrong pack, return it.' aisle_request_return returns an EIP-191 return request, signed via core request_wallet_sign [APPROVAL 2]. The backend verifies signer == payer and checks the policy window. 7) The merchant, in their own Claude, asks 'Any agent returns?' aisle_returns_inbox lists the request. 'Refund it': aisle_refund returns an EVM proposal USDC.transfer(payer, 9000000) with the original tx hash appended as a 32-byte reference [APPROVAL 3: merchant passkey], and the exactly-once check scans for that reference. 8) The buyer's aisle_receipt now shows 'Refunded, linked to 0x...'.
concepts.wow_moment: A tweet becomes a checkout. One passkey tap later, the merchant's MoonPay Commerce dashboard pings. Then the purchase is returned. The refund lands on Basescan with the original purchase hash embedded in its calldata, so the purchase and refund are linked on-chain for good: 'You just returned a stablecoin purchase.'
concepts.novel_mechanism: Returns for stablecoin commerce. Aisle implements, on MoonPay Commerce, the semantics of the unmerged x402 refund extension (PR #3681): a return window the merchant advertises in a domain-hosted manifest, a return request signed by the payer, and a merchant-funded refund whose calldata carries the original tx hash, with exactly-once enforcement. Around that sits three-way merchant verification (domain manifest, X handle, paylink id), a live-402 preflight that blocks price or payee drift, and the payerAddress interop fix. Together they turn a social post into a safe one-tap checkout.

concepts.backend_and_contracts: Hono on Railway with Postgres. Resolvers cover X syndication posts, the Helio public paylink GET (Origin header set server-side), and merchant manifests fetched from arbitrary domains, which is why that work lives in the backend: the plugin is capped at 16 hosts. The backend also decodes v1 and v2 402 challenges, screens with GoPlus, verifies receipts (Alchemy Base/Solana RPC plus Helio status), runs the return queue (viem verifyMessage, ERC-1271/6492-aware) and indexes refund references. No new contracts: refunds are plain USDC (0x8335...2913) transfers with reference bytes appended; on Solana, SPL TransferChecked plus Memo. Fallback rail if Helio's v2 402 doesn't work with plugin x402 proposals: pay the Helio charge as a Solana Pay transfer request (single-signer SPL transfer with a reference key). The builder runs a real Commerce store selling his motion-design LUT packs as demo merchant #1.
concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability: Buyer (the builder's PayBox account A) pays $9 via x402 to MoonPay Commerce, and the sweep sends it to the builder's own Commerce merchant wallet (account B), so it is recoverable. The return flow then sends it from B back to A. Net demo cost is Helio's fee plus Base gas (under $1). An optional purchase from a friendly third-party merchant is recovered through the same return flow. Hosting is about $5-10, for under $30 in total.
concepts.compliance: Non-custodial: the buyer pays the merchant through MoonPay Commerce, refunds come from the merchant's own wallet, and Aisle never touches funds. No card data and no merchant API keys; it uses only public paylink data, domain manifests and on-chain reads. That makes it multi-tenant without any credential pass-through. Merchants self-attest through their own domain. Payees are screened against sanctions with GoPlus. A category denylist (gambling, securities, regulated goods) applies, and merchants declare their regions in the manifest. Digital goods and services only, so no shipping PII. Return policies are the merchant's own and are shown before purchase. No MoonPay endorsement claims, and the tool text never says PayBox verified anything.
concepts.differentiation: First-party plugins are DeFi/trading. Curated x402 has Bitrefill, laso, AgentRes and BRIJ but no MoonPay Commerce client, and generic x402 calls omit payerAddress. Launch partners (Purch/Amazon, AgentRes/Resy, BRIJ) are single-merchant integrations, while Aisle opens the long tail of 6,000+ independent merchants on MoonPay's own rail. No x402 seller or agent wallet (Coinbase Agentic Wallets, Crossmint, Rye) offers returns. Watch-outs: PayBox's commerce_purchase approval type, the upcoming whop plugin, and Commerce's roadmap MCP server are all adjacent. Aisle is positioned as the agent client and returns layer that MoonPay could fold in.

Unpaid 402 preflight may create orphan pending payments
x402 needs a plain-EOA payer; EIP-7702-delegated wallets break it

Pitch Aisle to MoonPay as the Commerce agent client: stable schemas, swappable backend. Offer a web returns desk for merchants not on PayBox, with returns marked opt-in in the manifest. Seed the directory with the builder's store and 3-5 friendly merchants, then a GTM email to 6,000 merchants after judging.

concepts.why_it_wins_first: It is the most sponsor-native concept available: two MoonPay business units (PayBox and Commerce) in one passkey tap. It makes Commerce's 'already agent-payable' claim true inside Claude, ChatGPT and Grok, and adds the thing no x402 seller has: returns. The demo is native to X, the judging channel, and viewers can buy from the demo post, which counts as real traction. concepts.name: Landing
concepts.one_liner: The PayBox sell button. Tell your agent how much should land in your bank or PayPal, and one tap sends exactly the right USDC to a MoonPay deposit address that never passes through the chat.
concepts.target_user: PayBox users who hold USDC and need fiat: faucet and reward recipients, World winners, creators and merchants paid in USDC (for example via Greenlight or Aisle), and users in emerging markets (MoonPay quote currencies NGN, KES, MXN, BRL) paying rent or bills.
concepts.problem: PayBox has get_buy_link but no sell, although MoonPay's July 30 post promised you could 'onramp, convert, trade, offramp, and shop just by chatting'. Cashing out today means pasting a deposit address into a chat, which is the most dangerous thing an agent does (address substitution, prompt injection). Fees also make it hard to know how much will actually land.
concepts.hero_flow: 1) User: 'I need exactly $50 in my PayPal tonight.' 2) Core get_portfolio, e.g. 40 USDC on Base and 60 on Solana. 3) use_plugin landing_quote {target_fiat:50, currency:'usd', payout:'paypal', holdings}. The backend back-solves MoonPay's Get Sell quote for baseCurrencyAmount (e.g. 51.94 USDC on Solana: fees itemised, '$50.00 lands') and shows the spread against the ECB mid from api.frankfurter.dev. It checks sell availability for the user's country or state and picks the chain that already holds enough; otherwise it proposes core request_swap first. 4) landing_start {quote_id, wallet_address, chain}. The backend mints handle = externalTransactionId (UUIDv4) and returns an HMAC-signed MoonPay sell widget URL: baseCurrencyCode usdc_sol, baseCurrencyAmount, quoteCurrencyCode usd, refundWalletAddress = user wallet, redirectURL = backend/return/{handle}. The user confirms PayPal in MoonPay's hosted widget, where MoonPay runs KYC, geo checks and limits. MoonPay redirects to the backend with transactionId and depositWalletAddress. The backend cross-checks via 'Get Sell transaction by External identifier': amount, asset, status waitingForDeposit and refund address must match. 5) landing_send_sol {handle, sender} returns a Solana proposal: a single-signer SPL TransferChecked of exactly 51.94 USDC to the attested deposit ATA, with createAssociatedTokenAccountIdempotent if needed [APPROVAL 1: passkey]. On Base, landing_send returns USDC.transfer(deposit, amount). 6) landing_status {handle}: MoonPay status moves from waitingForDeposit to pending to completed; depositHash must equal the PayBox tx; then '$50.00 sent to PayPal' plus a journal line. Variant: World winnings go through first-party world redeem, then core request_swap, then Landing ('predict, win, cash out').
concepts.wow_moment: Minutes after a single passkey tap in Claude, the phone buzzes: PayPal, 'You received $50.00'. Solscan shows the USDC going straight to MoonPay, and nobody ever typed or pasted a deposit address.
concepts.novel_mechanism: Fiat-first, attested cash-out. The user states the fiat that must land; the backend back-solves MoonPay's live sell quote including fees and discloses the spread against the ECB mid. The deposit address arrives in MoonPay's redirect, bound to an unguessable externalTransactionId, and is cross-checked against MoonPay's API with the refund address pinned to the user's wallet. The plugin will only build one exact-amount transfer to that address. The LLM never sees or relays the address, so the cash-out is prompt-injection-proof by construction.

concepts.backend_and_contracts: Hono on Railway with Postgres (handles, quotes, attestations). MoonPay partner keys stay in the backend, which does HMAC-SHA256 URL signing and calls Get Sell quote, Get Sell transaction by External identifier (verified to exist at dev.moonpay.com/api-reference/widget/getselltransactionbyexternalid) and the off-ramp requote webhooks. A redirect endpoint captures depositWalletAddress, which the sell API does not expose. Rates come from Frankfurter (ECB mid), with Paycrest's keyless public rates as an NGN/KES benchmark. No contracts. The bundle holds 5 stable tools that call the backend and RPC; keys and hosts are config, editable after the upload lock.
concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability: The user's USDC goes directly to MoonPay's per-transaction deposit address, and MoonPay pays the user's own PayPal or bank; the builder never touches funds. A $50 demo returns about $47-49 to the builder's own PayPal, so it is recoverable minus MoonPay fees (roughly 1-4.5%) and network fees. If MoonPay can't complete the sale, funds return to refundWalletAddress. Hosting is about $5.
concepts.compliance: MoonPay (money transmitter licences in 46 states, NY BitLicense, MiCA via the AFM, FCA registration) performs KYC/AML, geo checks and payouts in its own hosted widget. The plugin never sees bank or PayPal details. Funds go from the user straight to MoonPay, so nothing is custodial or pooled. The partner keys belong to the builder and are brokered; no user credentials appear anywhere. Sell availability is pre-checked, and unsupported regions are refused, never routed around. Fees and spread are disclosed exactly, matching MoonPay's go-live rule that the quoted total must equal the final payment.
concepts.differentiation: Core PayBox has only get_buy_link and get_deposit_link, and no first-party plugin sells to fiat. The MoonPay CLI's virtual-account off-ramp isn't reachable from PayBox. concepts.name: Quorum
concepts.one_liner: Pledge the most you'd pay with one passkey tap. At close, a strategy-proof Moulin mechanism charges everyone the same lowest fair share, pays the organizer exactly the cost and returns each person's change on-chain. If the group doesn't form, everyone is refunded automatically.
concepts.target_user: PayBox users who chip in together: group gifts, group commissions, shared classes or charters, bulk orders. Also the organizers, creators and small merchants who sell fixed-cost or volume-priced goods to groups.
concepts.problem: Group purchases break down on coordination. Someone fronts the money and chases everyone (Splitwise only records the debt afterwards), early backers overpay, and refunds are manual when the group falls short. Mercata and MobShop died of exactly this friction in 2001. PayBox can't solve it today: every payment is single-payer and exact, x402 can't make the final price depend on who joins and can't return change, and plugins can't hold state or batch.
concepts.hero_flow:
Organizer, once: 'Start a Quorum: animated birthday video for Mark, $90 total, at least 3 people, closes Friday 6pm ET, pay me.' The agent calls quorum_create, which returns an EVM proposal on eip155:8453 for QuorumFactory.createPool(terms) with receiver = msg.sender. One approval, and the organizer gets a share link.
Participant (the hero):
1) User: 'I'm in for Mark's video, up to $40.' Agent runs discover_plugins (finds Quorum), then list_credentials (Base address and wallet_id).
2) use_plugin quorum_quote {pool, max:40, payer} (data). It returns the terms, 4 pledges so far, 'if it closed now: $22.50 each across 4', and a GoPlus screen of the organizer address. The plugin also recomputes your pledge escrow address itself (CREATE2 of keccak(pool, payer, max, deadline, nonce)) and lists its only two exits: pay the organizer at most your share, or refund you. Auto-refund after Saturday 6pm.
3) get_portfolio. If Base USDC is short, the agent uses get_buy_link (MoonPay to usdc_base) or request_swap.
4) use_plugin quorum_pledge with wallet_id returns an x402 proposal: POST https://api.quorum.<domain>/x402/pledge?pool=..&payer=..&max=40000000&n=.., maxAmount 40 USDC, Base, expires in 4 minutes.
5) PayBox fetches the live 402 (payTo = that term-bound escrow address) and opens the signing window. APPROVAL 1 (passkey). PayBox signs EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization. The backend checks from == payer and to == predicted address, then relays TBEFactory.settle(). The USDC lands in the escrow address, the clone deploys and registers in the pool. Paid response: escrow, tx hash, current standing.
6) The agent reads the result with get_request, then calls quorum_status (data), which re-reads Base: 40 USDC sits in your escrow, 5 pledges in the pool.
7) Friday 6pm: the keeper calls pool.clear(). Anyone can, via quorum_close (EVM proposal), and the organizer can close early once quorum is met. Pledges are $40/$35/$30/$25/$12 against $90. The largest group whose every member accepts the share C/k is the top 4, at $22.50 each. ONE transaction pays the organizer $90, returns $17.50/$12.50/$7.50/$2.50 of change, and refunds the $12 pledge in full.
8) quorum_receipt (data) decodes the clearing tx: 'You paid $22.50, the fair share across 4. $17.50 came back in tx 0x..'. The organizer delivers the video.
If quorum isn't met, clear() refunds everyone. After the hard deadline anyone can expire() a pledge; quorum_reclaim gives the payer an EVM proposal for it.
concepts.wow_moment: One Basescan transaction: the organizer receives exactly $90, each participant gets back their own, different change, and the person who couldn't afford the share is refunded in full. Nobody fronted money, nobody sent a reminder, and everyone tapped once.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
Moulin cost-sharing, which is group-strategyproof and budget-balanced, run as on-chain clearing over 'term-bound escrows'.
- Each pledge's x402 payTo is a CREATE2 address committing to (pool, payer, max, deadlines). A plain exact-scheme x402 payment from any client, PayBox included, therefore becomes a refundable, rule-bound escrow: one approval, no gas, and the server cannot change the terms.
- At close, the pool finds the largest set whose members all accept the equal share C(k)/k, charges exactly that, and refunds the change. This covers fixed-cost gifts and commissions as well as merchant volume tiers (C(k) = k·unitPrice(k), with unitPrice non-increasing).
- Reporting your true max is optimal, early joiners aren't penalized, and you approve a ceiling, never a price.
- Optional extension: an organizer-funded failure bonus (Tabarrok's dominant assurance contract).

concepts.backend_and_contracts:
Backend: Hono/TypeScript (Railway or Cloudflare Workers), viem, @x402/core and @x402/evm 2.28. It serves the 402 in v1 or v2, whichever PayBox accepts, with no side effects on unpaid probes. It self-facilitates settlement: verify the EIP-3009 signature, check from and to, then relay. A relayer EOA with about $5 of ETH on Base pays all gas. Postgres holds pool metadata, a keeper cron clears pools, and an optional public share page serves links (outside PayBox).
Contracts (Foundry, Base, USDC 0x8335..2913):
- TBEFactory: EIP-1167 clones at CREATE2(salt = keccak(terms)). settle() calls USDC.transferWithAuthorization(from, predicted, ...), then deploys and initializes the clone. deploy(terms) is permissionless in case someone front-runs the authorization.
- PledgeEscrow: three exits only. release(share) pays the receiver and returns the change to the payer; refund() pays the payer; expire() is permissionless after the hard deadline.
- QuorumPool: register() is permissionless; clear() sorts up to 32 pledges and finds the largest k whose k-th max is at least C(k)/k.
No admin keys and no upgrades. The semantics mirror Base AuthCaptureEscrow (0xf968..B19c). Its stock ERC3009 collector, though, needs ReceiveWithAuthorization with a paymentInfo-hash nonce, which an exact-scheme x402 signer like PayBox doesn't produce, so we need our own term-bound address. Tool schemas freeze at upload; curves, caps and wording live in the backend.
concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
Each pledge moves from the participant's PayBox wallet into that participant's own escrow address. It is never pooled and never sent to the builder. At clearing, the share goes to the organizer and the change goes back to the participant.
Demo: the builder is organizer and creator; 4 friends (or disclosed builder-owned wallets) pledge $12 to $40, about $142 in total, all of which returns within the group.
Irrecoverable spend: Base gas for deploys, settles and clears (under $2) plus about $5 of relayer ETH float, which can be withdrawn. Net cost is roughly $3 to $10. The builder's own exposure is at most one pledge.
concepts.compliance:
No custody:
- No admin keys, no upgrades, no pooled wallet.
- Each escrow can only pay its committed receiver (at most the cleared share) or refund its payer.
- Expiry refunds are permissionless.
- The server can't alter terms because they are hashed into payTo.

Other safeguards:
- The organizer is the seller of record and must have the rights to what they sell.
- Reward-style group purchase only: no equity, interest or lottery.
- GoPlus OFAC/phishing screen on organizer and payer.
- Pool titles are moderated; no PII on-chain.
- Beta caps: $100 per pledge, 32 pledges per pool.
- No credential pass-through: only the builder's RPC key, as a brokered header.
- Geo: organizers mark region-restricted pools, and tool text discloses smart-contract risk.
concepts.differentiation:
First-party World, Kamino, Jupiter, Sunrise, Aave and Hyperliquid are single-user DeFi or trading, and core request_transfer and pay_x402 are single-payer and exact-amount. Nothing coordinates several payers or settles to a variable price.
Curated x402 and launch partners (AgentRes, Purch, BRIJ) are single-buyer commerce. BRIJ's escrow intents cover one flight buyer.
Competitors:
- Splitwise: IOUs after the fact.
- Kickstarter, Juicebox, Gitcoin: fixed pledges, no fair-share change; Kickstarter is custodial.
- Groupon, Pinduoduo: merchant-set tiers, custodial, no truthfulness.
- Peanut, Request Network: single-payer.
- payload.exchange: a sponsor pays one user's 402.
- x402 auth-capture: single payer, needs a special signer, and no facilitator supports it.
key_risks: PayBox's live handling of a code-less CREATE2 payTo is untested end to end; only the proposal schema has been verified.
Custom escrow code holds real user funds.
Judges may read multi-party escrow as pooled funds or custody.
Demo logistics: 4-5 real PayBox users must pledge on camera.
Unknown PayBox paid-refetch timeout, x402 v1/v2 compatibility, and EIP-7702-delegated wallets that cannot pay x402.
The organizer might not deliver after clearing (ordinary seller risk).
concepts.mitigations:
Day-1 spike: one $1 pledge from a real PayBox wallet into a CREATE2 address on Base, recorded.
- Fallback: the same escrows funded by two EVM proposals (approve, then pledge) behind the same tool schema.
- Contracts under 250 lines, tested with Foundry fuzz and invariant tests (captured + refunded = deposited; only receiver or payer is ever paid), checked with Slither and open-sourced.
- One escrow address per pledge, with permissionless expiry, and tool text that names each escrow's two possible exits.
- Settle in about 3 s and return settlement status; idempotent retries; quorum_status finds an escrow by payer.
- Rehearse with friends' PayBox accounts.
- v2: a delivery-escrow stage released by a quorum of participants.

concepts.name: Brier
concepts.one_liner: Your agent buys an AI forecast with one tap. The fee waits in an escrow and the forecast is sealed on-chain before you pay. When Chainlink prints the result, a proper scoring rule splits the fee: the forecaster earns only for beating the market's odds, and you get the rest back.
concepts.target_user: PayBox users who trade or hedge with the first-party World plugin, or who want a decision-grade probability ('will ETH be above $X Friday?'). Also forecasters, starting with the builder's own engine, who want a track record nobody can fake.
concepts.problem: Paid predictions are a lemons market. x402 'picks' and 'edges' sell at flat prices with no accountability, about 11% of paid x402 endpoints don't deliver what they promise, and forecasters' track records can't be checked, so buyers pay the same for garbage as for alpha. In PayBox, World covers entering and settling a position, but nothing makes the 'price' step accountable.
concepts.hero_flow:
1) User: 'Will ETH be above $4,500 at 4pm ET Friday? Get a Brier forecast, max $2, before I decide on World.' Agent: discover_plugins (Brier), list_credentials. Optionally, the first-party World plugin's search, events and orderbook tools surface a related World market for context.
2) use_plugin brier_quote {asset:'ETH', strike:4500, resolve_at, max_fee:2, payer} (data).
- The backend canonicalizes the question to 'Chainlink ETH/USD on Base >= 4500 at the first round >= T'.
- It sets the baseline q = 38% from liquid public venues. The plugin fetches the same Polymarket gamma / Hyperliquid HIP-4 data live so the user can check it.
- It seals the forecast as h = keccak(p, salt). One sealed forecast per question bucket is sold to every buyer.
- It returns a payout table and the escrow address, recomputed in-plugin from the terms (payer, forecaster, fee, feed, strike, T, q, h).
3) use_plugin brier_buy with wallet_id returns an x402 proposal: POST https://api.brier.<domain>/x402/forecast?quote=..&payer=.., maxAmount 2 USDC, Base.
4) PayBox window. APPROVAL 1 (passkey). The backend relays settle() and the USDC lands in the forecast escrow. The paid response reveals p = 64%, the salt, 3 cited reasons and a signed receipt.
5) get_request, then brier_verify (data) reads Base and checks keccak(p, salt) == h: 'This is the forecast sealed before you paid. Edge vs market: +26 points.'
6) The user decides. Any trade goes through the first-party World plugin with its own approval, inside PayBox's geofence. Brier never trades.
7) At T, the keeper calls BrierSettler.settle(escrow, roundId, p, salt). Anyone can, via brier_settle (EVM proposal). The contract checks that the Chainlink round brackets T, sets the outcome o, and pays the forecaster F·clamp(1/2 + [S(p,o) − S(q,o)], 0, 1), where S(x,o) = 1 − (x − o)². The remainder is refunded to the buyer. If ETH is at least 4,500: forecaster $1.51, buyer $0.49 back. If below: forecaster $0.47, buyer $1.53 back.
8) brier_record (data) shows the forecaster's on-chain ledger of settled escrows and its skill vs the market.
concepts.wow_moment: The price prints and the fee splits itself on Basescan with no human judge: $1.51 to the forecaster because it said 64% when the market said 38% and was right, and $0.49 straight back to you. Every entry in the forecaster's track record is one of these transactions, so it can't be faked.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
Settling a purchase of information with a proper scoring rule.
- The payout is a Hanson market-scoring-rule trade from the market's probability q to the forecaster's p, subsidized by the buyer's fee.
- Pay rises only with skill over the market, and reporting your true belief maximizes expected pay. The rule is proper wherever it is unclamped, with k configurable.
- Commit-reveal blocks both free-riding and after-the-fact edits: the hash is in the escrow terms before payment, and the reveal is in the paid response.
- Resolution reads Chainlink on Base directly, so no one adjudicates.
- If the forecaster doesn't reveal by the deadline, the buyer gets a full refund.
- One sealed forecast is sold to many buyers and settled separately per escrow.
It fills x402's signed-offer, signed-receipt and delivery-guarantee gaps at once.

- BrierSettler: verifies the commitment; requires updatedAt(roundId) >= T and updatedAt(roundId-1) < T within a tolerance window, otherwise refunds; computes the payout in basis points; releases funds.
Feeds: Chainlink ETH/USD and BTC/USD on Base (addresses from data.chain.link). Tool schemas freeze at upload; question templates, k, fee levels and venues live in the backend.
concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
The fee ($1 to $5) goes from the buyer's wallet into a per-purchase escrow. At resolution it splits into a payout to the forecaster (the builder) and a refund to the buyer.
In the demo, the buyers are the builder's second wallet and friends, so the money is fully recoverable.
Costs: $0.05 to $0.30 of LLM and data per sealed bucket, under $1 of gas, and about $5 of relayer ETH float. Net irrecoverable spend is about $5 to $15.
concepts.compliance:
An information service priced by accuracy:
- The payout never exceeds the fee, and the buyer never receives more than they paid.
- No market positions, no order routing, no custody (code-bound escrow).
- v1 covers only crypto price questions resolved by Chainlink, with a minimum 1-hour horizon. No sports, casino or speed markets.
- Trades are a user-initiated handoff to first-party World, inside PayBox's geofence.
- 'Not financial advice' appears in every tool output.
- GoPlus OFAC screen on payers.
- No credential pass-through.
concepts.differentiation:
First-party World executes trades and Hyperliquid reads prices; neither forecasts or makes research accountable. Brier complements World and feeds into it.
Curated x402 and prediction sellers (predictionmarketspicks find_arbitrage, nfl_edge) charge flat fees with no accountability.
MoonPay's own moonpay-scout is an arbitrage scanner with stale fee assumptions. Dawn CLI does strategies and backtests, not paid accountable forecasts.
Trust and reputation layers rely on unpaid ratings. Metaculus and Good Judgment pay tournament prizes. LMSR uses scoring rules inside markets, not as the payment rule for buying a forecast.
No launch partner overlaps.
key_risks: Small fees can make the on-chain split look underwhelming.
An outcome-contingent payment may be read as wagering.
Oracle edge cases: Chainlink heartbeat, phase changes, stale feeds.
A weak engine settles low in public.
Free quotes seal forecasts before payment (an abuse and cost vector).
The demo needs a resolution moment on camera; thin markets can make the baseline manipulable.

Use $2 to $5 fees with k = 2 amplification, and show a motion graphic of the scoring curve.
- Framing: payout at most the fee, info only, no positions, minimum horizon, and World-only trade handoff.
- Round bracketing with a tolerance window, otherwise a full refund.
- Quotes cached per (asset, strike bucket, time bucket); one forecast sold to many buyers; per-payer rate limits.
- Baseline q is the midpoint of liquid venues, clamped to 5-95%, with its source committed in the terms.
- The demo pairs a live purchase with an earlier one that settles on camera.
- Macro questions with attested resolution only in v2.

concepts.name: Knock
concepts.one_liner: To reach a busy human, your agent posts a small bond with one tap. Reply, and it comes straight back on-chain. Mark it spam, and they keep it. Ignore it, and it returns at the deadline. Spam costs money; real messages cost nothing.
concepts.target_user: Senders: PayBox users whose agents need replies from busy people, for example to commission an artist, pitch a founder, file a bug with a maintainer or contact a landlord. Recipients: creators, maintainers, founders and journalists flooded by AI-written outreach, who can put a price on their attention.
concepts.problem: Agents make outreach free, so inboxes flood with AI-slop bug reports, mass applications and auto-pitches. Busy people close their DMs, and real requests get lost with the spam. Senders have no cheap way to prove they're serious, and recipients have no way to make spam pay. Earlier attempts (IronPort Bonded Sender in 2003, earn.com's paid email) were custodial Web2 systems built before agents.
concepts.hero_flow:
Recipient, once: Alice, an illustrator, says 'Gate my inbox with Knock: $5 bond, 72h window, forfeits to my Base wallet.' Her agent calls knock_inbox_setup (data), which returns a SIWE message; she signs it with core request_wallet_sign (EIP-191); knock_inbox_verify (data) binds her handle, verified email and payout address. Knock then publishes knock.<domain>/@alice, an x402 'doorbell' any agent can use.
Sender (the hero):
1) User: 'Ask @alice if she'd illustrate my book cover, budget about $800.' Agent: discover_plugins (Knock), list_credentials.
2) use_plugin knock_lookup {handle:'alice'} (data) shows a $5 bond and 72h window. It reads her record from Base: 37 bonds, 34 refunded, 8% forfeited, median reply 11h. Her payout address has been screened.
3) The agent drafts the message and the user approves the text. use_plugin knock_send with wallet_id returns an x402 proposal: POST https://api.knock.<domain>/x402/@alice?payer=..&exp=..&m=keccak(msg), JSON body {subject, body, from_name} up to 64 KiB, maxAmount 5 USDC, Base.
4) PayBox window. APPROVAL 1 (passkey). The backend moderates the message (rejected messages are refunded instantly) and checks from == payer. It then relays settle(): $5 goes into a bond escrow bound to (sender, Alice's payout address, $5, deadline, message hash). The email is delivered: '$5 bonded. Reply to return it. Spam? Keep it.' Paid response: knock_id, escrow, tx.
5) Alice replies from her verified address. A DKIM-verified inbound webhook triggers refund(): $5 goes back to the sender on Base, and the reply is forwarded to the sender.
6) get_request, then knock_status (data) verifies on-chain: 'Alice replied in 2h14m; your $5 came back in tx 0x..', plus her reply.
Alternatives: Alice taps 'Spam, keep it', or her own agent calls knock_verdict and signs an EIP-712 verdict via request_wallet_sign (no trusted operator). Either way she receives the $5. If nobody acts, anyone can call expire() after the deadline (knock_expire, EVM proposal) and the sender is refunded.
concepts.wow_moment: Alice's real Gmail shows a '$5 bonded' message. She replies 'Love it, send refs', and seconds later Basescan shows the $5 back in the sender's wallet. The next knock is AI slop: she taps 'Spam, keep it' and her wallet gets $5. Ignoring someone's agent now costs the sender, not the recipient.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
A deposit-refund system for attention: per-message bonds in term-bound x402 escrows, priced by the recipient.
- Three automatic exits: a DKIM-verified reply refunds the sender, a spam verdict forfeits the bond to the recipient, and silence refunds at the deadline.
- Recipients who hold a wallet sign EIP-712 verdicts, so they need no trusted operator.
- Forfeit rates are public on-chain, so senders' agents route around greedy recipients and the market disciplines both sides.
- The x402 doorbell means any x402 agent, not only PayBox, has to stake to knock.
- The message hash in the escrow terms means neither side can later dispute what was sent.

concepts.backend_and_contracts:
Backend: Hono/TypeScript with viem and @x402 2.28, self-facilitated settlement through a relayer.
- Inbox registry: SIWE plus an email magic link.
- LLM moderation before delivery.
- Outbound email from an authenticated domain (SPF/DKIM/DMARC, e.g. Postmark) and an inbound reply webhook that verifies DKIM.
- Keeper for expiries; message bodies deleted after the window.
Contracts (Foundry, Base):
- The shared TBEFactory.
- BondEscrow with terms (sender, recipient payout, amount, deadline, msgHash, judge). Exits: refund to the sender, or forfeit to the recipient.
- KnockJudge: accepts verdicts from the operator (for email-only recipients) or from the recipient's EIP-712 signature; expire() is permissionless.
Tool schemas freeze at upload; pricing, moderation and email templates live in the backend.
concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
Each bond moves from the sender's wallet into its own escrow. It then goes back to the sender (on a reply or silence) or to the recipient's registered address (on spam). The builder never holds it.
Demo: the builder sends $5 bonds to 2-3 friends who opted in, including one deliberate spam test. About $15 to $25 circulates and all of it returns.
Costs: email on a free tier, under $1 of gas, and about $5 of relayer float. Net irrecoverable spend is under $5.
concepts.compliance:
No unsolicited email: messages go only to inboxes whose owners registered and set a price.
- Sender identity (name and wallet) is shown, with CAN-SPAM-style headers and block lists.
- Harassment or illegal content is refunded before delivery.
- No custody: each escrow can only refund the sender or pay the committed recipient.
- Operator verdicts apply only to email-only recipients and are logged. Wallet recipients sign their own.
- The forfeit policy is disclosed before payment.
- Message bodies are deleted after the window; only hashes go on-chain.
- GoPlus OFAC screen.
- No credential pass-through.
concepts.differentiation:
None of the first-party plugins or core tools cover messaging or attention.
Curated x402: AgentMail sends email with no stake, which is complementary. The launch partners are unrelated.
Competitors:
- earn.com: custodial pay-for-reply, now shut down.
- IronPort Bonded Sender (2003): bulk mailers, centralized.
- HEY Screener: no money involved.
- Superpeer, Intro, Clarity: custodial paid calls.
- RentAHuman: custodial tasks with an 18% fee.
Knock is the first per-message, refund-by-default attention bond settled on-chain and payable by any x402 agent.
key_risks: Two-sided cold start: senders need bond-gated recipients, and recipients need senders.
Email deliverability and anti-spam law exposure.
Recipients forfeiting legitimate bonds; senders using paid messages to harass.
Email-only recipients depend on a trusted operator for reply detection and spam links.
Commerce-minded judges may read it as messaging rather than payments.
Same unknowns as the others: PayBox x402 compatibility and timeout, plus message privacy in the backend.
concepts.mitigations:
Recipients onboard with one chat message and one signature; seed 10-20 creators and maintainers before launch. Doorbell links work for any x402 agent and can go in bios and auto-replies.
- Opt-in delivery only, from an authenticated domain.
- Forfeit rate surfaced in knock_lookup.
- Per-sender rate limits plus moderation.
- EIP-712 verdicts remove operator trust for wallet recipients. The operator can only refund the sender or pay the committed recipient, and silence always refunds.
- The hero is an $800 commission inquiry, which keeps the story about commerce.
- Day-1 $1 x402 spike, same as the other concepts.

concepts.name: Homeline
concepts.one_liner: Pay the bill back home, not the cash. One sentence and one passkey tap put a real prepaid-electricity token on your family's meter in Nigeria, and your USDC is only taken once the token exists.
concepts.target_user: Nigerians abroad (UK, US, Canada) who send money home every month, mostly to keep the lights, TV and data on. Also Nigerians at home who hold USDC as a hedge against the naira but must go through P2P desks to pay any bill. The same tool inputs can later cover other prepaid-utility countries (Ghana, Kenya) through other bill-payment providers.
concepts.problem: Money sent home for bills loses value three times: the remittance fee, the exchange-rate spread and the recipient's cash-out fee. It may also never reach the bill. Prepaid electricity in Nigeria is bought in naira through local banks and apps that foreign cards and stablecoin holders struggle to use. PayBox can buy crypto with fiat but cannot sell it back. Its request_payment tool only creates USD cards locked to one merchant, which Nigerian billers don't accept and a plugin can't complete. No first-party plugin or curated x402 service sells utility tokens. Crypto payments can't be reversed, so paying a mistyped meter, or paying for a token the electricity company (DisCo) never issues, is a real loss. The PayBox approval window shows only raw transaction details, so the user can't spot either mistake.
concepts.hero_flow:
Host: the Claude.ai web connector, where the signing window appears immediately. Homeline is enabled as an unofficial plugin. The user types ONE sentence: 'Mum's light just finished - put N10,000 on her Ikeja Electric prepaid meter 45012345678 and text her the token on 0803 123 4567.'
1) The agent calls core list_credentials and picks the approved Base wallet (a plain EOA).
2) The agent calls use_plugin(homeline, quote_bill, {biller:'ikeja-electric', meter, meter_type:'prepaid', amount_ngn:10000, notify_phone, payer}) [data tool]. The plugin calls the backend's /v1/quote route with a brokered key. The backend calls VTpass merchant-verify, which returns the DisCo's own record for the meter: Customer_Name, Address, Meter_Type, Can_Vend, Min_Purchase_Amount and Customer_Arrears. The backend prices naira in USDC against a published reference rate (Paycrest's public rate), adds a 1% fee, checks the payer's USDC on Base and screens the address against sanctions lists. Output: 'Meter belongs to ADEB*** F*****, Allen Ave Ikeja, PREPAID, can vend. N10,000 = ~7.47 USDC (rate ~1,352, reference rate and spread shown). Delivered or not charged. Quote valid 4 min.' The tool description tells the agent that the PayBox window is the confirmation step, so no second chat turn is needed. If funds are short, readiness.next_action routes the agent to core get_buy_link (usdc_base), request_swap, or optionally first-party jupiter_withdraw_from_earn, paying over the Solana option.
3) The agent calls use_plugin(homeline, pay_bill, {quote_id}, wallet_id). It returns ONE io.paybox/transactionProposal of kind x402: chain eip155:8453, asset USDC, maxAmount 7470000 atomic units, POST https://api.homeline.xyz/v1/vend with body {quote_id}, expiresAt +240 s, plus an exact plain-language summary. PayBox fetches the unpaid 402, which has no side effects, checks asset and amount, and opens the transaction window.
4) APPROVAL #1, the only one: the user taps the passkey.
5) PayBox signs an EIP-3009 authorization and re-sends the POST. The Homeline server checks the authorization (signature, balance, unused nonce, single-use quote) and calls VTpass /api/pay. Only if VTpass returns code 000 'delivered' with a token and units does the server settle the payment on Base (transferWithAuthorization). It then returns 200 with {token, units, signed receipt, access_token} and texts the token to Mum. If the purchase fails, the server returns an error and never settles: the authorization simply expires and the user is not charged. If VTpass is still 'pending' after 5 s, the server settles, returns 'processing', and a worker refunds the USDC on-chain if the purchase finally fails.
6) The agent polls core get_request until it gets the paid response.
7) The agent calls use_plugin(homeline, confirm_delivery, {receipt, payer}) [data tool]. The plugin checks the receipt signature against a signer address set as a plugin environment variable. It reads the settlement transaction on Base over RPC and decodes the USDC Transfer (payer to Homeline, 7.47). It asks VTpass for the purchase status again. Result: 'Delivered - token 5571-2234-9081-4432-1180, units per DisCo, token issued 21:14:03, settled on Base 21:14:05, Basescan link'.
Visible outcome: in Lagos, Mum's phone buzzes with the 20-digit token. She types it into the meter keypad, the meter beeps ACCEPTED and the lights come on.
concepts.wow_moment: A pitch-dark Lagos sitting room. The meter beeps ACCEPTED, the lights and ceiling fan snap on, and the kids shout 'UP NEPA!' Then the reveal: an AI agent bought this light, approved with one passkey tap thousands of kilometres away. Basescan shows the USDC was taken seconds AFTER the DisCo issued the token.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
The payment settles only after the token is issued, and the user first sees who the meter is registered to.
(1) Before any tap, the DisCo's own records name the meter's registered owner (VTpass merchant-verify). That stops irreversible USDC going to a mistyped meter, a check the PayBox window can't show.
(2) Homeline uses x402 v2's default 'authorization' flow as a delivery guarantee. The server holds only the user's signed EIP-3009 authorization, buys the token, and settles on Base only if the token exists. Otherwise the authorization expires unused. This gives refunds without an escrow contract, filling x402's most-cited gap (refunds and escrow).
(3) A signed receipt ties the token, a hash of the meter number and the settlement transaction together, and the plugin re-checks it on-chain afterwards.
The result is a path from stablecoins to a real-world bill that skips cashing out altogether.

concepts.backend_and_contracts:
The plugin stays a thin stdio MCP bundle with 4 tools and fixed input formats. Everything that changes lives in a TypeScript Hono service on Railway or Fly and keeps evolving after the upload lock.
- x402 server: @x402/hono 2.28, serving both the v1 JSON and the v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED challenge formats. It checks the payment, runs the handler, then settles. Settlement happens on Base through viem from a relayer wallet funded with a few dollars of ETH, or through the PayAI/CDP /verify and /settle endpoints.
- Biller: VTpass. Checked 2026-10-17: POST /api/merchant-verify returns Customer_Name, Address, Meter_Type, Can_Vend, Min_Purchase_Amount, Customer_Arrears and commission_details. POST /api/pay for prepaid returns token, purchased_code, units and tokenAmount. POST /api/requery checks a past purchase. Sandbox meter numbers simulate pending, timeout and failure. 12 DisCos are documented. Baxi, Flutterwave Bills and Reloadly Utilities can be swapped in as alternative providers.
- Reference exchange rate: Paycrest's public rates endpoint (no key needed).
- SMS: Termii, with WhatsApp as fallback; the token is always shown in chat too.
- Postgres (Neon) stores quotes (single-use), receipts and duplicate-request keys. Receipts are EIP-712 signed by a KMS key whose address is a plugin environment variable.
- A refund worker re-checks pending purchases and returns USDC to the authorization's sender.
- Optional: a ~30-line Solidity ReceiptLog on Base emitting BillPaid(receiptHash, settlementTx) for family records.
No contract ever holds user funds.
hosts_needed: api.homeline.xyz (builder backend: quotes, x402 purchase endpoint, receipts, purchase status). Data routes use a brokered Bearer key; the x402 route is authorized by the payment itself.
base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com (Base RPC for checking settlements, brokered Authorization: Bearer key)
concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
The user's USDC on Base goes to Homeline's builder-owned wallet, but only after the token is issued. The builder periodically converts USDC to naira to refill a prepaid VTpass wallet, and VTpass pays the DisCo, which issues the token to the family's meter. Homeline earns VTpass's reseller commission (returned in commission_details) plus the 1% fee.
In the demo the builder pays his own service, so every USDC comes back to his wallet. The only real spend is electricity his family would buy anyway (about N10k-30k, roughly $7-22), plus cents of Base gas for settlements and refunds. Failed purchases are never settled; slow failures are refunded on-chain. Total out-of-pocket is well under $30 and almost entirely recoverable.
concepts.compliance:
No custody: the user's USDC stays in their wallet until a real token exists, and nothing is pooled.
Homeline is the merchant of record. It sells a prepaid utility token, a product like a voucher, through an established Nigerian bill-payment provider. It delivers no cash and exchanges no currency for customers: the token is priced in USDC, with the rate and fee shown before the tap.
No user credentials pass through: only builder-owned keys on the backend or in brokered headers.
Location-aware: only supported Nigerian billers; payer addresses are screened against sanctions lists before purchase; per-address caps (e.g. at most $50 per purchase and $200 per day) act as the merchant's own risk limits; prepaid only at launch, with postpaid disclosed as a later feature.
Personal data: the meter and phone number are used only to buy the token and send the SMS. Names are masked in outputs and phone numbers are not logged.
Honest wording: 'units as calculated by the DisCo (net of VAT)' and 'delivered, or not charged / refunded'. Tool text never claims PayBox verified anything, only the plugin's own on-chain checks.
concepts.differentiation:
First-party plugins are all DeFi or trading (World, Aave read-only, Kamino, Jupiter, Hyperliquid read-only spot, Sunrise); none touch bills.
Core tools: get_buy_link is buy-only, with no way to sell back to fiat; request_transfer only moves crypto; request_payment creates USD cards that Nigerian billers won't accept.
Curated x402 services: Bitrefill sells gift cards, eSIMs and airtime, with no meter check and no pay-on-delivery. laso sells a US prepaid card. Launch partners AgentRes, Purch and BRIJ cover restaurants, Amazon and flights.
The research's 'Send Home' remittance idea delivers cash and needs Paycrest business verification or MoonPay partner keys. Homeline pays the bill directly, so there is no cash-out step.
Remittance apps (LemFi, Sendwave) are human fiat apps, not agent-native. No known x402 seller settles only after a real-world delivery.
key_risks: PayBox's timeout for the paid x402 re-fetch is undocumented, and a slow DisCo response could exceed it.
VTpass live-account onboarding (ID checks), prefunding and its reseller terms; a DisCo outage during filming.
Regulatory optics: judges may ask whether paying bills from USDC counts as money transmission.
PayBox x402 compatibility (v1 vs v2 challenges, POST bodies) and EIP-7702-delegated wallets, which must be converted back to plain accounts before paying.
Nigerian SMS sender-ID registration can delay delivering the token by text.
Exchange-rate moves between quote and purchase.
concepts.mitigations:
Give the paid handler a hard 5-second limit for the purchase. Success means settle; a clear failure means don't settle; still pending means settle, return 'processing', and let the status-check worker refund on-chain automatically. All three paths can be rehearsed with VTpass's sandbox pending and timeout meter numbers.
Serve both v1 and v2 402 formats, test them early in the developer portal, and pre-test the exact PayBox wallet.
Keep providers swappable (VTpass, Baxi, Flutterwave Bills, Reloadly) behind the fixed plugin tool formats, so billers and countries can change in the backend after the upload lock.
Present Homeline as a prepaid-product merchant with caps, sanctions screening and disclosures, prepaid only.
Always show the token in chat, so SMS is a convenience rather than a dependency.
Use 4-minute quotes with a small rate buffer. Film several takes, and show the 'not charged' failure path on camera as proof of the guarantee.

concepts.why_it_wins_first:
Neeraj Prasad says people will come to PayBox 'because their AI can finally finish the job'. Here the job is turning the lights back on, on camera, with one tap and an explorer receipt.
Against the inferred rubric:
- Usefulness: a monthly need for millions of Nigerians abroad and stablecoin-holding Nigerians at home. MoonPay's sell widget already quotes NGN.
- PayBox-native depth: one x402 approval that only settles when the token is delivered; routes shortfalls to get_buy_link, request_swap or first-party Earn; checks the result on-chain afterwards.
- Originality: settle-after-delivery plus DisCo-confirmed meter ownership closes x402's refund gap without an escrow contract.

It is also visibly human-made: the builder's own family and his own country. concepts.name: Paper Trail
concepts.one_liner: Agents can't lick stamps. Now they don't have to. Say it, preview the exact card or letter, tap once, and a real postcard or certified letter is printed and mailed with a QR that proves on-chain what was sent, when, and which wallet paid.
concepts.target_user: Anyone whose agent gets stuck on a paper-only task: cancelling a gym or lease that requires written or certified notice, mailing a dispute or formal notice, or sending a card to a grandparent who doesn't use email. Also small businesses mailing thank-you cards or overdue-payment notices from chat.
concepts.problem: Agents can draft any letter but can't put it in a mailbox. Paper still controls important tasks (cancellations, notices, disputes) and personal ones (cards for relatives who aren't online). Print-and-mail APIs exist but need an account, a card and an integration, so no agent can buy from them. Proof of mailing is weak: a certified-mail receipt proves an envelope moved, not what it said. And with rogue AI agents in the headlines, nobody can tell from a piece of paper whether a human actually authorised it.
concepts.hero_flow:
Host: Claude.ai web connector. The user types ONE sentence: 'Mail Grandma the sunflower postcard - Happy 80th, Mama Ade, I'll be home for Christmas. Love, Dami - to 12 Oak Lane, Dayton OH 45402.'
1) The agent calls core list_credentials and gets the Base wallet.
2) The agent calls use_plugin(papertrail, preview_mail, {kind:'postcard_6x9', design:'sunflowers', message, to:{...}, payer}) [data tool]. The backend checks the address with the print provider, runs content moderation and creates a free TEST print with the provider that is never mailed. It returns front and back proof images plus a PDF, with a reserved box showing where the QR will go. It also returns 'deliverable', the price (1.50 USDC), the delivery estimate, a salted content hash of the exact proof (everything except the QR box), and a single-use quote_id valid 4 minutes and tied to that hash.
3) The agent calls use_plugin(papertrail, send_mail, {quote_id}, wallet_id). It returns ONE x402 proposal: eip155:8453, USDC, maxAmount 1500000, POST https://api.papertrail.xyz/v1/send with {quote_id}. Summary: 'Paper Trail will print exactly proof 7c1e... and mail it USPS First-Class to A. Ade, Dayton OH, for 1.50 USDC; refunded if it can't be mailed.'
4) APPROVAL #1, the only one: passkey tap in the PayBox window.
5) The server checks the payment, settles on Base (tx A) and quickly returns {job_id, access_token, settlement_tx, verify_url}. In the background, the builder's operator wallet calls MailNotary.anchor(contentHash, txA, jobId) on Base (tx B). The server then prints the QR (linking to papertrail.xyz/v/{id}) into the reserved box and sends the live order to the provider. If the provider rejects it, the USDC is refunded on-chain automatically.
6) The agent polls core get_request for the paid response.

concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
The user's USDC on Base goes to Paper Trail's builder-owned wallet at settlement. The builder's card pays the print provider per piece (roughly $0.7-1.2 per postcard, $1-2 per letter and $7-9 for certified mail in the US). Rejected or undeliverable pieces are refunded on-chain from the builder's wallet. Recording each content hash costs about $0.001-0.01 of Base gas.
In the demo the builder pays his own endpoint, so the USDC is fully recoverable. The only irreversible spend is printing and postage for about 10 test pieces ($15-30). Previews are free in test mode.
concepts.compliance:
No custody: the user pays for a service, and refunds happen only when delivery fails. The builder is the merchant of record.
Content rules and moderation: no threats, harassment, hate, impersonation or bulk unsolicited marketing. Each wallet has a daily cap, and letters must carry a return address for accountability.
Personal data: addresses go only to the print provider, are masked in tool output, are never logged, and are deleted after delivery. Only salted hashes go on-chain, never names, addresses or content.
Location-aware: only countries the provider supports, none under sanctions; payer wallets are screened against sanctions lists.
Honest claims: the chain proves this wallet paid for this exact content at this time. The 'a human approved it' claim rests on PayBox requiring owner approval for every plugin payment, and the verification page says that rather than claiming cryptographic proof of a passkey. Not legal advice; certified tracking comes from USPS.
concepts.differentiation:
Nothing in PayBox touches physical mail. First-party plugins are DeFi. Among curated x402 services, AgentMail and Merit's stableemail only send email. Launch partners cover restaurants, Amazon and flights.
Print-and-mail APIs (Lob, PostGrid, Stannp, Click2Mail) can't be paid by an agent and offer no proof of content. USPS Certified proves the envelope moved, not what it said.
Unlike 'agent buys X' shopping demos, the value is the self-proving paper and the payment tied to the exact preview. It also answers this month's rogue-agent fears with a physical object showing a wallet-signed, owner-approved payment.
key_risks: The print provider's onboarding and card payment from the builder's country; senders outside the US may need PostGrid or Stannp. Free test-mode proofs, USPS Certified and international support are assumed from Lob's public API and need confirming.
Physical delivery takes days, so the hero piece must be mailed in advance and someone at the destination must film its arrival.
Abuse (harassing or fraudulent letters) and exposure of personal data through chat.
PayBox's timeout for the paid request.
Being seen as a novelty unless the certified-notice use case is shown.
concepts.mitigations: Put providers behind an adapter so the backend can switch after the upload lock. Mail the hero postcard early and film its arrival. Enforce strict moderation, caps and the return-address rule, and never log personal data or put it on-chain. Keep the paid handler fast (check payment and settle only; everything else runs in the background). Show both the emotional postcard and the 'cancel my gym by certified letter' scene in the demo. Use free test-mode previews so iteration costs nothing.

concepts.name: Roll Credits
concepts.one_liner: Commission a short film from one sentence with a capped USDC budget and one passkey tap. The studio renders it, sends your change back on-chain, pays every human artist in the film instantly, and prints all those transactions into the end credits.
concepts.target_user: AI filmmakers, creators and small brands making 15-30 second videos (promos, tributes, crypto satire in the spirit of the Lumara AI Film Festival's 'Rekt' award) who juggle subscriptions to several AI models. Also the human musicians and designers whose work ends up in AI films.
concepts.problem: Making an AI short film today means a separate subscription or credit pack for each model, unclear spending, and paying for failed generations, with no licence or record of where the content came from. The humans whose music, title design or sound effects end up in the film rarely get paid. An agent could coordinate it all, but approving every paid call would mean dozens of taps. PayBox's x402 payments are exact amounts only, so 'pay up to X' budgets aren't possible. And the Creative category has no coverage in PayBox's plugin catalog or curated x402 list.
concepts.hero_flow:
Host: Claude.ai web connector. The user types ONE sentence: 'Make a 20-second trailer about me buying the top of SOL in 2021 - Lumara Rekt Award energy. $4 max.'
1) The agent calls core list_credentials and gets the Solana wallet.
2) The agent calls use_plugin(rollcredits, pitch, {brief, length_s:20, style:'noir-trailer', budget_cap_usdc:4, payer}) [data tool]. The backend writes a 4-shot storyboard, prices each shot at current provider rates and picks licensed human-made assets (a musician's score, the builder's title sequence, a sound-effects pack). It returns storyboard frames and an itemised budget: AI rendering ~2.10, human royalties ~0.80, studio fee 0.30, expected change ~0.80. It also returns a pitch_id valid for 4 minutes.
3) The agent calls use_plugin(rollcredits, greenlight, {pitch_id}, wallet_id). It returns ONE x402 proposal: solana:mainnet, USDC, maxAmount 4000000, POST https://api.rollcredits.xyz/v1/greenlight with {pitch_id}. The summary states the cap, the refund rules and who gets paid.
4) APPROVAL #1, the only one: passkey tap.
5) The server checks the payment, settles (Solana tx A), queues the render and returns {job_id, access_token, eta}.
6) The agent polls core get_request for the paid response. Optionally, use_plugin(rollcredits, dailies, {job_id, access_token}) shows progress per shot; a failed shot is re-rendered at the studio's cost or refunded.
7) The backend renders the shots in parallel (fal, Venice) and assembles them with the builder's hand-made title, colour-grade and credits templates. It then sends the on-chain payouts: royalties to each human contributor (USDC transfers C1 to C3) and the unused budget back to the payer (tx R). Only then does it render the end credits with every transaction signature, and embed a C2PA content-credentials record (AI disclosure, models used, prompt hash, payer, settlement tx, licence).
8) The agent calls use_plugin(rollcredits, screening, {job_id, access_token}) [data tool]. It returns the film URL, licence receipt and money ledger, and checks transactions A, R and C1-C3 over Solana RPC.
Visible outcome: the film plays, the end credits roll with real transaction signatures, and the musician's phone buzzes with his royalty.
concepts.wow_moment: Cold open on a striking noir shot, then the end credits roll, and every line is a transaction: 'BUDGET APPROVED BY PASSKEY - 4.00 USDC - 3jK9...', 'CHANGE RETURNED - 0.62 USDC', 'ORIGINAL SCORE - TOLU A. - PAID 0.40 USDC'. Cut to Tolu's phone buzzing in his home studio seconds after the film finished rendering.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
The credits are the receipts.
(1) 'Pay up to X' budgets on PayBox's exact-amount x402 payments: the user approves a cap once, the studio charges actual cost and automatically sends the change back on-chain, and failed shots cost nothing.
(2) Instant pay for humans: every human-made asset in the film (score, title design, sound effects) has a wallet and a licence, and is paid on-chain from that same single payment as soon as the film renders.
(3) The full money trail (settlement, change, royalties) is printed into the film's end credits and its C2PA content credentials, so the film carries its own audit trail and AI disclosure.
One approval replaces dozens of separate model payments without asking the user to approve each one.

concepts.name: Landed
concepts.one_liner: The sell button PayBox is missing: one gasless passkey tap turns USDC into naira, shillings or dollars in a real bank or mobile-money account, and the money only leaves your wallet if the payout order is still live at that instant.
concepts.target_user: PayBox users who earn or hold USDC but pay their lives in local currency. First, freelancers, remote workers and crypto earners in Paycrest's live corridors (Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania; bank, mobile money and M-Pesa phone/Till/Paybill), plus the relatives they support. Next, once MoonPay enables partner keys, US/EU/LatAm users cashing out to bank, PayPal or Venmo through MoonPay sell.
concepts.problem:
PayBox can fund a wallet (core get_buy_link) but cannot turn USDC back into spendable money. Core tools and all six official plugins are on-ramp or DeFi only, even though MoonPay's 30 Jul 2026 launch post said PayBox agents can 'onramp, convert, trade, offramp, and shop just by chatting'. MoonPay CLI has a bank off-ramp but no mobile-money payout, and it is not in PayBox.

Demand is proven. The two biggest x402 sellers by revenue are cash-equivalents: Bitrefill took $589k and Laso $115k in 7 days (whatagentsbuy). Agents already pay markups and 4+ separate approvals to turn stablecoins into spending power. Today users leave the chat for a P2P desk or exchange.

A naive 'transfer to the deposit address' inside PayBox fails in practice:
- EVM proposals need ETH for gas.
- A slow passkey approval (approvals live about 10 min) can land funds in an expired LP order and force a refund round-trip.

The corridors are real and live. On 16 Oct Paycrest quoted 1,352.32 NGN and 128.57 KES per USDC, with payouts to banks, mobile money and M-Pesa Paybill/Till.
concepts.hero_flow:
1. User in Claude.ai (PayBox connector): 'Send NGN 50,000 to my GTBank account 0123456789.'
2. Agent calls core list_credentials and get_portfolio: Base USDC 62.10, 0 ETH. No approval.
3. Agent calls use_plugin(landed.quote_payout, wallet_id) with {amount:'50000', amount_in:'fiat', currency:'NGN', rail:'bank', institution:<GTBank code from list_corridors>, account:'0123456789', payer_address, chain:'eip155:8453'}.
   - The backend calls Paycrest /v2/rates, verify-account and a reference rate in parallel.
   - It returns the verified account-holder name, 37.04 USDC to send, the rate against the reference with the spread in bps, fees, ETA, limits, and a quote_id with a 3-minute rate lock. No approval.
4. User confirms the name and amount. Agent calls landed.create_payout {quote_id, refund_address: payer}. The backend POSTs /v2/sender/orders with source.refundAddress set to the user's wallet and returns an opaque high-entropy payout handle. No approval.
5. Agent calls landed.pay_payout {handle, payer_address}. The plugin returns ONE io.paybox/transactionProposal of kind x402: POST https://api.landed.<tld>/v1/payouts/{handle}/settle, chain eip155:8453, USDC, maxAmount 37040000, expiresAt now+4 min.
6. PayBox fetches the live 402 (payTo = Paycrest providerAccount.receiveAddress, amount = amountToTransfer) and opens the transaction window. APPROVAL 1: passkey (Face ID).
7. PayBox signs EIP-3009 and replays the request. The backend runs the x402 v2 authorization flow:
   - facilitator /verify;
   - handler checks that the Paycrest order is still pending and unexpired, the amount matches, and the live rate is within the lock;
   - facilitator /settle: CDP submits transferWithAuthorization on Base and pays the gas;
   - backend returns {order_id, settle_tx, status}.
   If any check fails, the backend returns 409 and nothing settles. The user is not charged, and the agent re-quotes.
8. Agent polls core get_request, then calls landed.track_payout {handle}. The plugin reads the settle tx on Base directly (Alchemy) and the Paycrest status from the backend (settled, LP tx hash). It reports 'NGN 50,000 delivered to GTBank ****6789 (<verified name>), tx 0x...'.

Visible outcome: the GTBank credit SMS arrives on the phone. BaseScan shows USDC moving from the user's wallet to the LP deposit address with 0 ETH spent by the user.

Branches:
- Kenya: M-Pesa phone, Till and Paybill bills use the identical flow.
- MoonPay sell (when enabled): landed.start_moonpay_sell returns a MoonPay-hosted link where MoonPay handles KYC and bank details. The redirect captures depositWalletAddress, and the same pay_payout x402 tool pays it.
- Fallbacks: pay_payout_solana returns a single-signer SPL transfer. pay_payout_gateway returns Paycrest Gateway approve and createOrder EVM proposals for EIP-7702-delegated wallets.
- Composition: 'cash out from my savings' first runs the first-party kamino or jupiter withdraw tool.
concepts.wow_moment: About 90 seconds after a single Face ID tap, from a wallet holding zero ETH, a real 'Credit Alert NGN 50,000.00' SMS lands on the builder's phone. BaseScan shows the USDC going straight from the wallet to the deposit address, with gas paid by the facilitator. In a second take, a quote approved after its lock expired is refused with 'you were not charged'.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
x402 as a non-custodial payout rail with verify-then-settle.

The backend's 402 challenge names a licensed liquidity provider's single-use deposit address as payTo: Paycrest providerAccount.receiveAddress, or MoonPay's sell depositWalletAddress. The user signs one EIP-3009 authorization that moves funds straight from their wallet to the LP. The facilitator pays the gas, and the builder never touches the money.

x402 v2's default 'authorization' flow runs the handler between verify and settle. At that moment the backend re-checks LP order liveness, the exact amount and a rate lock. Human approval latency (proposals up to 5 min, approvals about 10) therefore cannot strand funds in a dead order or at a stale rate: a late authorization is simply never settled.

The paid HTTP response is the payout receipt. Post-transaction verification reads both the chain and the LP status, which covers what PayBox's raw-bytes window cannot show.
