concepts.backend_and_contracts:
Plugin: one dist/plugin.mjs with 8 zod-4 tools whose schemas are frozen at upload. All volatile logic lives in the backend, so it can keep evolving after the upload lock (hosts, vars and secrets stay editable).

Backend: Hono on Cloudflare Workers or Vercel.
- x402: @x402/hono, @x402/evm and @x402/svm 2.28 (v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED/PAYMENT-SIGNATURE headers), default 'authorization' flow. The handler checks order liveness and the rate lock before settle. The 402 path is side-effect free, with a static $0.50 sample challenge for portal validation.
- Facilitator: CDP (KYT/OFAC, fee-free on Base), with PayAI as fallback.
- Paycrest Sender API v2 under the builder's KYB'd sender account: POST /v2/sender/orders (amountIn crypto|fiat, source.refundAddress, optional disclosed senderFeePercent), GET /v2/sender/orders/:id, /v2/rates, verify-account and institutions. Webhooks are HMAC-verified (X-Paycrest-Signature).
- Gateway fallback: Paycrest createOrder, with messageHash RSA-encrypted server-side from GET /v2/pubkey so the sender key never leaves the server.
- MoonPay sell: HMAC URL signing and redirectURL capture, once partner keys are granted.
- Reference FX: api.frankfurter.dev for EUR/MXN/BRL. For NGN/KES, the Paycrest buy/sell mid plus a second public source.
- Upstash Redis REST: handles, idempotency, per-wallet caps, and encrypted PII purged by TTL.

No custom contracts.

concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
Funds move from the user's wallet to the Paycrest receiveAddress via an EIP-3009 authorization relayed by the facilitator, which pays gas. A licensed LP then pays the recipient's bank or mobile money. The builder never holds funds, and expired or failed orders refund to source.refundAddress (the user).

Demo cost: 3-4 cash-outs of $5-25 into the builder's own NGN bank or Opay accounts, about $60 total. That money is recoverable as naira, minus roughly 0.5-1% spread and LP fees (about $0.60 in total). The CDP facilitator is fee-free, and no ETH is needed.

Fixed costs: a domain (about $10), plus a business-name registration if KYB requires one (about $10-20).

Optional revenue: a disclosed Paycrest senderFeePercent (for example 0.3%).
concepts.compliance:
Custody: none. Funds go from the user's wallet straight to a licensed LP's single-use deposit address, and refunds return to the user. No pooled funds, no user credentials, no card data.

Screening: the builder is a KYB-verified Paycrest sender; Paycrest places compliance holds; the CDP facilitator screens every payer (KYT/OFAC).

Geo controls:
- Corridor allowlist: NG, KE, UG and TZ via Paycrest; MoonPay sell only where MoonPay supports sell.
- The agent confirms the user's residency, and sanctioned jurisdictions are blocked.
- Self-payouts are the default; third-party sends are capped.

Limits: $0.50-$500 per order and a daily cap per wallet. The recipient's account name is shown and confirmed before paying.

Disclosure: rate, reference rate, spread in bps, fees and ETA, never framed as 'interest'.

PII: account numbers are minimised, encrypted at rest, purged after settlement and never logged. With MoonPay sell, KYC and bank details stay inside MoonPay.
concepts.differentiation:
First-party plugins (world, aave, kamino, jupiter, hyperliquid, sunrise) are DeFi or trading, and core has get_buy_link but no sell. Landed is the only path from USDC to a bank or mobile wallet inside PayBox.

Curated x402 services (Bitrefill gift cards, Laso prepaid cards) are cash-equivalents with markups and multi-step approvals. The launch partners (AgentRes, Purch, BRIJ) are commerce, not cash-out.

Other options all fall short:
- MoonPay CLI's bank off-ramp has no mobile money and is not in PayBox.
- Paycrest's own consumer app, exchanges and P2P desks force users out of the chat.
- Coinbase Agentic Wallets and FluxA offer no African bank or mobile-money payouts.

Landed routes to MoonPay's own sell rail wherever MoonPay serves, and to Paycrest where it doesn't (mobile money, Paybill/Till, family payouts). That turns PayBox's loop into buy, hold, sell.
key_risks: Paycrest sender KYB is required for both the API and Gateway paths; a solo builder needs a registered business name or hackathon sender access
Untested: PayBox x402 against a v2 server whose payTo is a third-party deposit address
LP order validity (validUntil) and rate drift against human approval time
Compliance optics: the builder is sender of record for family remittances
MoonPay may not grant partner keys, which delays the US/EU sell rail
EIP-7702-delegated wallets cannot pay x402 without an undelegate step
Any network whose deposits require a memo cannot use x402, because EIP-3009 has no memo field
Facilitator settle can fail after verify if the payer moves funds in between
The demo needs the builder's own account in a supported corridor, or MoonPay sell
concepts.mitigations:
KYB: start on day 0, either by registering a sole-proprietor business name or by asking Paycrest for hackathon sender access.

PayBox interop: run a $1 end-to-end test (x402 paying a receiveAddress through PayBox) before building anything else.

Dead orders: verify-then-settle plus a 3-minute rate lock refuse dead or drifted orders with a 409, so nothing is charged. source.refundAddress returns any stray deposit to the user.

Compliance: corridor allowlist, amount caps, residency confirmation and CDP KYT. Self-payouts are the default and third-party sends are gated.

MoonPay keys: a rail abstraction lets MoonPay sell switch on in the backend with no tool-schema change.

Delegated wallets: a Solana transfer, or Gateway approve plus createOrder.

Memos: route x402 only to memo-less Base/Solana USDC orders.

Settle failures: retry settlement and surface 'settlement_pending' with the tx hash.

Demo: use the builder's own NGN accounts, or MoonPay sell to their own bank.

concepts.why_it_wins_first:
It fills the most obvious hole in PayBox: you can buy, but you can't sell. Demand is in the corpus: agents already spend about $700k a week on cash-equivalents (Bitrefill plus Laso) to get the same result badly. It delivers on MoonPay's own 'offramp' promise, and every MoonPay-served corridor can route back to MoonPay sell.

Few entrants will clear real-world payout rails to show money landing in a bank. The outcome is therefore rare and instantly legible: a credit alert on camera plus an explorer hash.

The mechanism is new. x402 becomes a gasless payout rail, and verify-then-settle means approval latency can never strand funds. The flow is one approval and non-custodial, with explicit geo and compliance controls, which the judges of a licensed money transmitter will notice. The builder narrates a corridor they actually use, which proves the work is human-made.

Repeat use is built in: every payday, bill and family transfer. Volume flows to MoonPay's sell rail and the LP network, with an optional disclosed sender fee.

concepts.name: Payable
concepts.one_liner: Verified invoices any AI agent can pay in one tap. Funds go straight to the issuer's wallet, a look-alike fake is refused before anyone approves, and the same invoice can never be charged twice.
concepts.target_user: Freelancers, agencies and small businesses that bill in USDC, including merchants displaced when Coinbase Commerce shut down on 31 Mar 2026, and the AI agents of the clients who pay them. The payer tool also serves anyone paying an existing MoonPay Commerce paylink, Solana Pay QR or EIP-681 link from chat.
concepts.problem:
The PayBox catalog has zero merchant tooling: no invoicing, merchant-side acceptance, refunds or reconciliation. x402 itself has no invoice semantics either: no payee identity, no exactly-once guarantee and no receipts. Plugin proposals also cannot attach the payment-identifier extension or custom headers.

MoonPay Commerce's 6,000+ merchants are 'already agent-payable', but standard x402 clients omit the mandatory payerAddress, and Commerce's MCP server and ACP support are still on its roadmap. Coinbase Commerce's shutdown displaced merchants who now need a new way to get paid.

The two classic accounts-payable losses get worse when an agent pays:
- fake invoices with swapped or look-alike payees (x402 audits already found a payee that differed from its listing);
- duplicate payments.

The October 2026 'rogue agent' news makes businesses wary. MoonPay bought Entendre in June specifically for agentic reconciliation and bookkeeping, and Visa is piloting an MCP server that creates invoices and payment links from natural language.
concepts.hero_flow:
Issuer side (Claude.ai, wallet A, 'Demi Studio'):
1. 'Invoice Acme $25 for the logo, due Friday.' The agent calls use_plugin(payable.issuer_challenge) with {address A, domain 'demi.studio'} and gets an EIP-4361 message plus optional DNS TXT proof instructions.
2. The agent calls core request_wallet_sign {op:'message'}. APPROVAL 1: a one-time issuer verification that yields a 24-hour token.
3. The agent calls payable.create_invoice {signature, amount:'25', chain:'eip155:8453', memo, due, client:'Acme'}. The backend verifies the signature (ERC-1271/6492-aware) and the DNS TXT record, and binds payTo = A to this issuer. It returns https://pay.payable.<tld>/i/7f3k and a ready-to-send message. No approval.

Payer side (a second Claude.ai window or ChatGPT, wallet B, 'Acme'):
4. A phishing look-alike arrives first (demi-studio.co, payTo 0xA1..f00). payable.inspect_link returns 'Unverified issuer; payTo imitates a verified Demi Studio wallet; domain not bound'. The agent refuses, and no proposal is ever built.
5. The user pastes the real link. payable.inspect_link returns 'Demi Studio, issuer verified (wallet + demi.studio), $25.00 USDC on Base, due Fri, unpaid, first payment to this payee'. No approval.
6. The agent checks core get_portfolio. If funds are short, core get_buy_link opens MoonPay Guest Checkout (Apple Pay) to top up.
7. The agent calls payable.pay_link {url, payer_address B}. It returns ONE x402 proposal: POST https://pay.payable.<tld>/i/7f3k/pay, USDC on Base, maxAmount 25000000. APPROVAL 2: passkey.
8. Backend: facilitator /verify, then an atomic invoice lock (Upstash SET NX), then /settle, which moves funds from B directly to A. It marks the invoice paid and returns 200 with an EIP-712 receipt signed by the backend.
9. The agent polls core get_request, then calls payable.verify_receipt {receipt}. It checks the signature and the on-chain AuthorizationUsed/Transfer log and returns 'Paid, receipt #..., tx 0x...'.
10. 'Pay it again': inspect_link shows paid, so the reply is 'Already paid at 14:02, no payment proposed'. Even a raw replay through core use_service gets a 409 before settlement, so no charge.

Issuer side:
11. 'Who paid this week? Export for my accountant.' payable.books {token} returns a reconciled ledger: invoice -> payer -> amount -> tx -> journal line (Dr USDC / Cr A/R). The agent exports the CSV to Google Sheets via the Drive connector.

The same pay_link tool also pays:
- MoonPay Commerce paylinks (x402 POST api.hel.io/v1/x402/checkout/{paylinkId}?payerAddress=...);
- Solana Pay transfer URIs (Solana proposal with reference key and memo);
- EIP-681 links (EVM proposal).

payable.refund returns an EVM USDC transfer from the issuer's wallet back to the payer (one approval), linked to the invoice.
concepts.wow_moment: Live on mainnet, the client's agent refuses a pixel-perfect fake invoice because its payee only imitates the verified issuer's wallet. It then pays the real invoice with one Face ID tap, and the USDC lands straight in the freelancer's wallet on BaseScan. An immediate 'pay it again' comes back: 'already paid at 14:02, no charge'.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
Invoices are x402 resources with exactly-once, verify-then-settle semantics and issuer-bound payees.

Each invoice URL serves a 402 whose payTo is the issuer's own wallet. The issuer has proven ownership of that wallet with a SIWE signature (and optionally of a domain via DNS TXT), so any payer agent can check who it is paying before an approval even exists.

On payment, the server verifies the EIP-3009 authorization, then takes an atomic invoice lock and settles only if it wins the lock. Duplicate, late or replayed payments are never settled, so the payer is never charged. This replaces x402's payment-identifier extension, which plugin proposals cannot attach.

The 200 response is an EIP-712 receipt that verify_receipt checks against the on-chain log. Because the links are plain x402, any client can pay them (PayBox core use_service, Coinbase, FluxA). The plugin adds identity, books and refunds.

- Human pay page on GET /i/{id}: wallet connect and Solana Pay QR.
- MoonPay Commerce interop: paylink/charge metadata is fetched server-side, and the x402 target is api.hel.io.
- Ledger with CSV and journal export.

concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
The payer's wallet pays the issuer's wallet directly; the facilitator relays the payer's EIP-3009 authorization and pays gas. Refunds go from issuer to payer by the issuer's own approval. The builder is never in the flow of funds.

Demo cost:
- $25-50 cycled between the builder's two PayBox wallets: 100% recoverable, and the facilitator is fee-free.
- A $1 dynamic paylink on the builder's own MoonPay Commerce account: recoverable.
- Under $1 of Base ETH for the refund.

Later revenue comes from issuer features (verified-domain badge, accounting exports), never from a cut of funds in flight.
concepts.compliance:
Custody: none, by construction. payTo is the issuer's own wallet and the builder never touches funds, so this is not money transmission.

Credentials: no per-user API keys or credentials, only the builder's facilitator credentials. Issuer identity comes from a wallet signature plus optional DNS proof, with no PII required.

Data: invoice fields are minimal and the client name is optional. No card data is handled. Receipts and exports are records, not tax advice.

Screening: the CDP facilitator screens payers (KYT/OFAC), and issuer addresses are sanctions-screened.

Commerce payments follow MoonPay Commerce's own rules: paylinks with required customer fields are not paid.

Geo: neutral peer-to-business USDC on Base/Solana.
concepts.differentiation:
No first-party plugin or core tool issues invoices or verifies payees. Core pay_x402/use_service can pay a 402, but it knows nothing about issuer identity, invoice state, duplicates or receipts, and it omits Commerce's mandatory payerAddress.

Curated x402 services are sellers, not invoicing tools, and the launch partners (AgentRes, Purch, BRIJ) are consumer commerce.

MoonPay Commerce requires merchant KYB and API keys, and its MCP server is still roadmap. Payable is the 30-second long-tail front door that also pays Commerce links, adding to Commerce GMV rather than competing.

Other options:
- Request Network needs approve plus pay and an x-client-id.
- Coinbase Commerce is closed.
- Stripe and Cloudflare x402 acceptance is US-only and requires merchant onboarding.
- Visa's invoice MCP server is an enterprise pilot.

Judges may read it as competing with MoonPay Commerce
Look-alike detection false positives or negatives
PayBox may show a 409 after signing as a failed payment, even though nothing was charged
Untested: Commerce x402 v2/payerAddress interop, and the 10 req/60 s per-IP limit behind shared PayBox egress
Extra issuer signature prompt
Outcome is less visceral than a bank alert

Look-alikes: conservative rules that warn and require explicit confirmation. An unverified first-time payee is never paid silently.

Commerce interop: $1 Commerce test on day one.

concepts.name: Payrun
concepts.one_liner: One passkey pays the whole team: a single Solana transaction settles a wallet in Lisbon, a bank in Lagos and M-Pesa in Nairobi, and every payslip verifies on-chain.
concepts.target_user: Small teams, startups, agencies and DAOs that pay contractors in several countries from a USDC treasury, especially African teams paying local staff in naira or shillings. Also families who support several relatives.
concepts.problem:
PayBox plugin proposals are single calls with no batching, so paying N people from chat means N proposals and N passkey taps. The corpus notes the only way around this is a pre-existing splitter contract.

Teams paying contractors abroad also need local currency (naira, shillings), and no PayBox tool provides it. Streaming-payroll tooling is decaying: Sablier entered maintenance mode in Jul 2026, and Superfluid needs three setup transactions (approve, upgrade, setFlowrate).

Payouts are a job MoonPay already recognises: Deel is a MoonPay Enterprise Pay Out customer. Payroll treasuries have won agent hackathons (ArcFlow at Arc HackMoney 2026, and payroll was highlighted in Coinbase's Agents in Action recap).

Yet nothing does a human-approved, one-approval, mixed-rail payroll run from chat.
concepts.wow_moment: One Face ID tap, one Solana signature, and three phones on the table buzz in sequence: a GTBank credit alert in Lagos, an M-Pesa SMS in Nairobi and a Phantom +40 USDC notification. Solscan shows all three transfers inside the same transaction.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
One signature, many rails.

The backend compiles a single-signer Solana v0 transaction whose recipients mix ordinary wallets with licensed LPs' single-use deposit addresses. Crypto and fiat payees therefore settle from one approval despite PayBox's no-batching rule. A 'payrun:<id>' memo makes every run reconstructable from the chain alone, so history needs no plugin state.

On Base, a 25-line PayrunBatch contract only ever calls transferFrom(msg.sender, ...). A standing allowance can therefore only be spent by the owner's own call, and every run after setup costs one approval.

Payslips bind the payee, local amount, rate, chain tx and LP settlement tx, and they verify against the chain. This is the post-transaction proof that PayBox's raw-bytes window cannot give.

concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
Wallet payees are paid directly from the payer's wallet. Fiat payees are paid from the payer's wallet to LP deposit addresses, and the LPs pay out to the payees' banks or M-Pesa. The builder never holds funds, and expired fiat legs refund to the payer.

Demo cost: about $60 split across the builder's own GTBank account, a second bank or Opay account (or a friend's M-Pesa, sent back) and the builder's Phantom wallet. It is recoverable minus about 1% spread, about $0.40 of non-recoverable token-account rent, and under $0.01 in fees. The Base contract deploy costs under $0.10.
concepts.compliance:

Screening: KYB'd Paycrest sender; every wallet payee is screened for sanctions and phishing flags (GoPlus); bank and mobile-money account names are matched before paying.

Limits and geo: per-run caps, and a corridor allowlist for fiat legs.

Scope: contractor and family payouts only, with no employment or tax advice.

Data: team-book PII is encrypted, SIWE-gated and deletable. FX and fees are disclosed per payee. Above thresholds, Travel-Rule data is passed through Paycrest's source/destination KYC fields.
concepts.differentiation:
Core sends one transfer per approval, and no first-party plugin pays people. Curated x402 services do not pay out.

Other options:
- Disperse-style splitters are crypto-only, non-agentic and still need approve plus disperse.
- Deel, Rise and Request Finance payroll are off-chat SaaS with onboarding.
- Sablier is in maintenance, and Superfluid needs three setup transactions plus USDCx.
- The treasury and DCA agents MoonPay judges have already seen do not pay humans in local currency.

Payrun is the only one-approval, mixed-rail (wallet + bank + mobile money) payout run from chat.

Untested: whether Paycrest's Solana receiveAddress is an owner address or a token account, and whether deposits need a memo (if so, two fiat legs cannot share one transaction)

concepts.name: Keyframe: pay-on-delivery motion studio
concepts.one_liner: Commission a real motion-design piece from chat. One gasless passkey tap pays USDC into an escrow address that does not exist yet and whose address IS the deal. The studio can only collect by publishing the key that decrypts your file, and a missed deadline refunds you with zero taps.
concepts.target_user: Founders, creators, crypto projects and small brands who already use PayBox in Claude/ChatGPT. They need short-form motion assets for X (launch stings, kinetic captions, animated charts, vertical promos) and don't want to trust an unknown seller with prepayment. Second-order users: any x402 seller who wants to offer buyer protection through the same escrow middleware.
concepts.problem:
Creative is the only track with zero first-party coverage, and the curated x402 set has no generative media. Paying for slow, fallible work over x402 is unsafe:
- x402 'exact' payments are final, and refunds are unstandardized: auth-capture v1.1 has no facilitator support and the refund extension is an unreviewed PR.
- About 11% of judgeable paid x402 endpoints under-deliver.
- Renders take minutes, while PayBox ends the plugin sandbox before payment.
- Escrow via AuthCaptureEscrow costs 2-3 approvals plus permit/EIP-3009 typed data that break on EIP-7702-delegated wallets.
- PayBox's window shows only raw payee bytes, so the user cannot tell what they are paying into.
concepts.hero_flow:
1) User: 'Make a 12-second vertical launch sting for Ripcord, navy and orange, budget $3.'
2) The agent calls core list_credentials (Base wallet 0xU), then use_plugin (with wallet_id) keyframe_quote {brief, 1080x1920, 12s, buyer: 0xU} [data].
   - One backend call content-screens the brief, prices it ($2.40, ETA ~3 min, deadline +20 min), mints a per-order secret K and builds terms T = {buyer, seller, USDC, 2.40, keyHash = keccak(K), deadline, salt}.
   - The plugin derives escrow E = CREATE2(factory, keccak(T), runnerInitHash).
   - It reads eth_getCode(0xU). An 0xef0100 prefix means 7702-delegated, so it routes to the direct rail.
   - It reads the Base USDC balance. On a shortfall it returns the exact amount and tells the agent to call core get_buy_link.
   - Output is a quote card: 'pay into 0xE5c... (no code yet; its rules are its hash)'.
3) The agent calls keyframe_commission {quote_id, buyer} [x402 proposal]: POST https://api.keyframe.studio/v1/orders, body {quote_id, buyer}, chain eip155:8453, asset Base USDC, maxAmount 2400000, expiresAt now+4 min.
4) PayBox fetches the live 402 (served as v1 body and v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED; amount 2.40, payTo = E) and checks asset and amount. APPROVAL 1/1: passkey. PayBox signs EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization(0xU to E) and retries.
5) The backend self-facilitates. It checks from == T.buyer, to == E and value == 2.40, submits the authorization (its relayer pays gas), queues the render and returns 200 {order_id, access_token (256-bit bearer handle), E, T, settlement_tx}.
6) The agent polls core get_request to terminal, then passes the paid response to keyframe_verify [data]. The plugin recomputes E from T, decodes the settlement receipt's USDC Transfer log (0xU to E, 2.400000) and confirms E has no code and holds 2.40. It reports: 'Your 2.40 USDC sits at 0xE5c.... It can only reach the studio if the key whose hash is 0x9ab... is published before 18:20 UTC; after that it can only return to you, and anyone can trigger that.'
7) The render worker runs the builder's motion template system, encrypts the master with K, uploads the ciphertext plus a watermarked preview, then calls factory.release(T, K, contentHash). A runner is CREATE2-deployed at E, pays the seller and self-destructs in its constructor (EIP-6780), so E is empty and reusable.
8) The agent calls keyframe_status {order_id, access_token} [data], the bearer-handle poll. It returns the preview, the MP4 URL and the release tx. The plugin decodes the Released event and checks keccak(K) == keyHash and sha256(file) == contentHash. It reports: 'Delivered. The studio was paid by publishing the key that decrypts your file. Even if our server vanished, that on-chain key plus the public ciphertext still gets you the file.'
   VISIBLE OUTCOME: the finished sting, ready to post.
9) Failure branch:
   - Order #2 misses its deadline. The keeper calls factory.refund(T), which is permissionless, and the USDC returns to 0xU with 0 approvals.
   - If the keeper is down, keyframe_refund returns the same call as an evm proposal.
   - If the studio rejects a brief, factory.void(T) refunds instantly.
concepts.wow_moment: Basescan shows 2.40 USDC sitting at an address with no contract. Minutes later, the studio's payout transaction carries, in plain calldata, the key that decrypts the video now playing full-screen. Then the second order misses its deadline, and the money returns to the PayBox wallet without anyone tapping anything.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
Counterfactual x402 escrow, with payTo set to a CREATE2 address computed from the hash of the deal terms.
- PayBox's documented check is asset and amount only, so PayBox's own gasless EIP-3009 x402 flow funds an escrow that doesn't exist yet. That takes one tap and needs no approve, no permit and no facilitator support.
- The escrow materializes only to settle: a deploy-and-self-destruct runner whose only possible recipients are the seller or the buyer.
- Seller: hash-locked. Anyone presenting K before the deadline triggers payment to T.seller.
- Buyer: after the deadline (anyone can trigger) or on seller void.
- This gives x402 auth-capture semantics (escrow, void, refund) on the plain exact scheme.
- It makes the raw payee in PayBox's window self-authenticating, because the address proves the terms.
- It turns delivery into a fair exchange of access for payment: 'the receipt is the key'.
- The same factory is one-line middleware for any x402 seller.

concepts.backend_and_contracts:
CONTRACT: KeyframeEscrowFactory on Base (Foundry, verified, immutable, ownerless, no fees).
- computeAddress(Terms).
- release(Terms, key, contentHash): anyone presenting K with keccak(K) == keyHash before the deadline; funds can only go to T.seller.
- void(Terms): seller only; instant refund.
- refund(Terms): anyone, after the deadline. Also usable any time after settlement for late or duplicate funds.
- A minimal Runner init code reads its single instruction from the factory via EIP-1153 transient storage, transfers USDC and self-destructs in its constructor, so every escrow address stays stateless and reusable.
- Per-order cap $50.
- Testing: fuzz and invariant tests ('funds at E only ever reach T.buyer or T.seller') plus a Halmos symbolic check.

BACKEND: Hono on Cloudflare Workers.
- Quote API.
- x402 resource server (@x402/core + @x402/evm 2.28) emitting a per-order payTo, serving both the v1 body and v2 headers.
- Self-facilitation through a low-balance relayer, with the PayAI facilitator as fallback.
- D1 for quotes and orders, with a deterministic quote_id so PayBox's approval-time re-fetch gets a byte-identical 402.
- R2 for ciphertext and previews.
- Cron Trigger keeper for deadline refunds.
- Alchemy address-activity webhook for the direct-transfer rail.

RENDER WORKER: a Cloud Run container running the builder's HyperFrames/ffmpeg template system (human-designed type, color and easing), with AES-256-GCM per-order keys.

PLUGIN: thin starter-1.0.2 MCP server; every tool is one bounded fetch of 4 s or less.

concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
Buyer USDC (the builder's PayBox wallet) goes to the counterfactual escrow. From there it goes to the builder's studio wallet on delivery, or back to the buyer on deadline or void. Every demo dollar ends in a wallet the builder controls.
- A float of about $15-20 is recycled across 5-8 live test orders.
- Irreversible spend: Base gas for settlement, release and refund (about $0.01 each; about $2 total including contract deploy), render compute (cents) and free tiers (Workers, Alchemy).
- Total exposure is under $25, and about 95% is recoverable.
concepts.compliance:
- Non-custodial by construction: the escrow is an immutable, ownerless CREATE2 address. Neither the builder nor the relayer can redirect funds; they can only reach T.buyer or T.seller per the terms.
- No credential pass-through: the plugin never sees keys, backend/RPC keys are brokered headers, and SIWE grants read access only.
- The x402 plain-EOA rule is respected: delegated wallets are detected up front and routed to a single-call EVM transfer instead of failing mid-approval.
- The backend screens the buyer address for sanctions (GoPlus) before issuing a 402.
- Content policy is screened at quote time, before money moves. Only human-designed templates and user-attested assets are used, with no likeness of real people.
- Digital service: no geofence needed. The builder is merchant of record.
- The contract is unaudited but tiny, capped, formally tested and source-verified. This is disclosed in plugin text and never presented as 'PayBox-verified'.
concepts.differentiation:
- First-party plugins (world, aave, kamino, jupiter, hyperliquid, sunrise) are all DeFi/trading; none are creative and none do escrow.
- The curated x402 set (80 endpoints) has no generative media. Uncurated StableStudio is pay-upfront, needs a SIWX signature (an extra passkey) to poll, and its result URLs expire in about 20 minutes. Venice needs SIWX and a $5 minimum top-up.
- Launch partners AgentRes, Purch and BRIJ do bookings and shopping. BRIJ's escrow-backed intents are flight-specific on Solana; Keyframe's escrow is a generic x402-on-Base primitive.
- AuthCaptureEscrow 'EscrowPay' designs need 2-3 approvals and an operator.
- RentAHuman is custodial with an 18% fee.
- Single-model AI video wrappers are a kill-list cliché. Keyframe sells the builder's own human-designed motion system, and its escrow is a new primitive rather than a wrapper.
key_risks: PayBox plugin x402 interop with a self-hosted server whose payTo changes per order (unverified until the first live test)
Judges reading it as 'yet another AI video generator'
Unaudited escrow contract invites custody questions
Fair exchange guarantees access, not quality: a seller could reveal the key to a poor file
Render latency or failure during the recorded demo
Keeper downtime or relayer gas exhaustion delaying refunds
PayBox's x402 approval sheet may render payTo opaquely
concepts.mitigations:
- Day-1 live $0.10 order through the Test console and Validate transaction. Serve both v1 and v2 challenges. A deterministic quote_id keeps the approval-time re-fetch identical.
- Lead the demo and repo with the builder's own design system and template craft (visibly human-made).
- Keep the contract at about 80 lines, ownerless, with a per-order cap, invariant and symbolic tests, verified source and a published threat model.
- Show a watermarked preview before release, and emit contentHash in the release event as dispute evidence. An optional review-window variant is available.
- Pre-warm the render container, and pre-record a clean take with explorer proof.
- Refund is permissionless, with the buyer-side keyframe_refund fallback. The relayer is topped up with alerting, with PayAI as fallback facilitator.
- keyframe_quote and keyframe_verify print the CREATE2 derivation so the payee shown in the window is independently checkable.

concepts.why_it_wins_first:
It is the rare entry that is all four of these at once:
1. In the empty Creative track, with a product the builder owns rather than a wrapper.
2. A genuinely new payment primitive that closes x402's most-cited gap (refunds and escrow) using PayBox's own gasless x402 flow, without waiting on facilitators.

concepts.name: Quorum: PayBox as your multisig co-signer
concepts.one_liner: Make your PayBox wallet a Safe/Squads signer that reads before it signs. The plugin independently decodes every pending treasury transaction, binds your passkey to the exact hash, and signs and executes with one single-call proposal: no EIP-712, no blind signing.
concepts.target_user: Startups, DAOs, agencies and crypto-native merchants whose operating money sits in a Safe (Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon) or a Squads v4 vault (Solana), and whose signers already work in Claude/ChatGPT with PayBox. Also families running a 2-of-2 'two-person rule' savings Safe.
concepts.problem:
Multisig signing is where the largest losses happen. Bybit's signers approved a Safe transaction their UI misrepresented: a delegatecall that rewrote the Safe's implementation slot, about $1.5B lost.
- Signers approve 32-byte hashes they cannot read, and mobile signing is painful.
- Inside PayBox, a plugin cannot request EIP-712 signatures at all, and the transaction window shows only raw calldata.
- Teams adopting agents need a guarantee that no single agent or human can move treasury money, given October 2026's 'rogue agent' news.
concepts.hero_flow:
1) User: 'Anything waiting for my signature on the team treasury?'
2) The agent calls core list_credentials (EVM 0xU, Solana member key) and use_plugin quorum_inbox {owner: 0xU, member} [data].
   - The plugin lists Safes owned by 0xU and their pending multisig txs from api.safe.global/tx-service/{base, eth, arb1, matic} (brokered Bearer), plus Squads proposals via Solana RPC.
   - Each gets an independent decode and a risk grade.
   - '#41 Base Safe 0x7a..: MultiSendCallOnly -> 3 USDC transfers (400/400/400) to known contractors, 1 of 2 confirmations (Alice signed in the Safe app), LOW.'
   - '#42: operation=DELEGATECALL to unverified 0x96.. writing storage slot 0 (masterCopy). CRITICAL, do not sign (Bybit pattern).'
3) User: 'Open #41.' The agent calls quorum_inspect {chain, safe, nonce} [data].
   - Recomputes safeTxHash from the raw fields (EIP-712 domain = chainId + Safe address, SafeTx struct, nonce) and checks it equals the Transaction Service hash.
   - Decodes the MultiSend sub-calls with viem.
   - Simulates from the Safe with alchemy_simulateAssetChanges to get exact token deltas.
   - Checks each recipient against the Safe's own executed history (first-time payee; first/last-4-character lookalike = address poisoning) and against GoPlus.
   - Prints the hash to cross-check in the Safe app.
4) User: 'Sign and pay.' The agent calls quorum_execute [evm proposal]: {to: Safe, value: 0, data: execTransaction(to, value, data, operation=1 to canonical MultiSendCallOnly, safeTxGas, baseGas, gasPrice, gasToken, refundReceiver, signatures)} on eip155:8453.
   - signatures = Alice's EIP-712 signature from the TS plus {r = 0xU, s = 0, v = 1} (Safe's 'approved by msg.sender' type), sorted by owner address.
5) PayBox simulates. APPROVAL 1/1: passkey. PayBox signs, broadcasts and confirms.
6) The agent calls quorum_verify {tx_hash} [data]. It decodes ExecutionSuccess(safeTxHash), the 3 USDC Transfer logs and the new Safe nonce: 'Paid alice 400, bob 400, carol 400 USDC; #42 still blocked.'
   VISIBLE OUTCOME: contractor balances change on Basescan.
Variants:
- If the user is not the last signer, quorum_approve returns a single approveHash(safeTxHash) call: an on-chain confirmation with no typed data.
- For Squads v4, quorum_squads_execute returns ONE single-signer v0 Solana tx containing proposal_approve + vault_transaction_execute. Inner SPL transfers are decoded, and BPF-loader program upgrades are flagged CRITICAL.
concepts.wow_moment: Live, the plugin turns the Bybit attack into a red line: 'this routine-looking upgrade delegatecalls an unverified contract that rewrites your Safe's implementation slot. Do not sign.' Then one Face ID tap both co-signs and executes the real payroll, and three contractor balances update on Basescan. The approved hash matches the one shown in the Safe app character for character.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
Uses Safe's on-chain approval path, approveHash plus the v=1 'approved hash / msg.sender' signature type inside execTransaction. A PayBox wallet can then confirm and execute multisig transactions with ordinary single-call EVM proposals.
- This legitimately routes around the rule that plugins cannot request EIP-712, with no sign-and-relay workaround.
- It works even for EIP-7702-delegated wallets.
- Every approval is bound to a safeTxHash recomputed from raw fields, independently of the Safe UI (the 'second UI' that would have stopped Bybit).
- Asset deltas are simulated before the tap.
- On Solana it is mirrored with single-signer Squads v4 instructions that approve and execute in one transaction, so both of PayBox's wallet families are first-class co-signers.

concepts.backend_and_contracts:
No new contracts by design. It uses the audited Safe v1.3/1.4.1 singletons, MultiSendCallOnly, and Squads v4 (SQDS4ep65T869zMMBKyuUq6aD6EgTu8psMjkvj52pCf).

BACKEND: Hono on Cloudflare Workers.
- Decode service: Sourcify/Etherscan-v2 ABI resolution, plus a canonical Safe deployment registry so that a delegatecall to MultiSend/MultiSendCallOnly reads as normal and anything else is CRITICAL.
- Risk rules authored by the builder: owner/threshold/module/guard/fallback-handler/singleton changes, unlimited approvals to unknown spenders, first-time payees, address-poisoning lookalikes vs the Safe's own executed history, value anomalies, GoPlus sanctions.
- Simulation via alchemy_simulateAssetChanges and eth_call with state overrides.
- Squads message decoder (@sqds/multisig).
- Signature packing and owner sorting.

The plugin stays a thin MCP server. Heavy decoding runs server-side inside the 4 s fetch budget and is cached per safeTxHash.

concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
No money flows to the builder at all.
- Demo setup: a 2-of-3 Safe on Base (owners: the PayBox wallet plus two builder wallets) funded with about $30 USDC, and a 2-of-3 Squads vault on Solana with about $15.
- Payouts go to the builder's own 'contractor' wallets. The staged Bybit-style tx is never executed.
- Irreversible cost: Safe deployment (about $0.05), execTransaction/approveHash gas (about $0.01 each) and Solana fees. Squads rent is recoverable.
- Under $50 is parked, and about 99% is recoverable.
concepts.compliance:
- Purely non-custodial tooling for the user's own multisig. The plugin never signs, never holds keys and never moves money except through PayBox proposals the user approves, each of which is one of the user's own multisig signatures.
- No credential pass-through: the Safe API key is the builder's brokered header, and no user secrets are involved.
- Not a financial product (no yield, trading or credit), so no geofence is needed. GoPlus sanctions hits surface as blocking warnings.
- All copy is framed as the plugin's own analysis, never as a PayBox-verified preview, consistent with the docs' 'tool text is untrusted' rule.
- It reinforces PayBox's stated principle: 'the agent orchestrates, it does not authorize'.
concepts.differentiation:
- No first-party plugin touches multisig: aave and hyperliquid are read-only, and the rest are Solana DeFi.
- Core request_wallet_sign can only blind-sign typed data, and plugins cannot request it. Quorum adds decoding, hash binding and simulation, and its hero path needs no typed data at all.
- Nothing in the curated x402 set or among the launch partners covers treasury operations.
- The Safe{Wallet} and Squads apps are the single UI whose compromise caused Bybit; Quorum is an independent second decoder.
- Browser-wallet transaction scanners are not chat-native and cannot co-sign from PayBox.
- Unlike spend-policy/guardrail layers (kill list), Quorum doesn't restrict agents. It makes human co-signing legible and one-tap.
key_risks: Narrower audience: requires an existing Safe/Squads and adding the PayBox wallet as an owner
Safe Transaction Service plan and rate limits (the unauthenticated tier is 2 rps / 5k requests per month)
Judges may file the risk engine under 'another guardrail layer'
Decode and simulation edge cases (nested MultiSend, delegatecall simulation, proxies)
A Squads approve+execute tx can exceed 1,232 bytes for large inner transactions
Executing a stale nonce, or a tx another owner executes first
concepts.mitigations:
- Ship a 'two-person rule' template (2-of-2 family or founder Safe) and a one-message 'add PayBox as a signer' guide. Lead the pitch with co-signing and paying; the risk grade is supporting evidence.
- Paid Safe API key via brokered header, caching per safeTxHash, and an on-chain fallback (ApproveHash events + nonce) if the TS is down.
- Conservative defaults: any delegatecall outside the canonical MultiSend set is CRITICAL, and unknown proxies get implementation-slot reads.
- For Squads, split approve and execute, or use address lookup tables, when over 1,232 bytes.
- Re-read the Safe nonce and confirmations immediately before building the proposal. PayBox's pre-sign simulation safely reverts stale or duplicate executions.
- The builder's security rules and decode design are documented in the repo (visibly human-made).

concepts.name: Brier: forecasts that refund you when they're wrong
concepts.one_liner: Accountable prediction-market research inside PayBox. Ask whether a market is fairly priced and pay $1 with one gasless tap. Your forecast is committed on-chain in the same transaction as your payment, and at expiry a Chainlink-settled Brier score decides how much of your fee the forecaster's own collateral pays back.
concepts.target_user: PayBox users who trade World prediction markets (or watch Kalshi, Polymarket and HIP-4) and want a priced, accountable second opinion before they enter. Also anyone burned by paid 'signals' that keep the fee whether right or wrong.
concepts.problem:
In PayBox, World already covers 'enter', but 'price' and 'settle' remain unaccountable.
- Paid forecasts and signals keep the fee whether right or wrong, and track records are cherry-picked after the fact.
- Venues disagree on fees and resolution rules; MoonPay's own scout skill still assumes a 2% Polymarket fee.
- x402 sellers give no outcome guarantees, and buyers cannot prove a forecast existed before the outcome.
- Trading from a plugin runs into EIP-712, per-user secrets and IP geoblocks, so the useful open job is honest pricing and settlement.
concepts.hero_flow:
1) User: 'World has ETH >= $4,000 at 20:00 UTC at 44c YES. Is that fair?'
2) The agent reads the market through the first-party World plugin, then calls use_plugin brier_consensus {feed: ETH/USD, strike: 4000, expiry: 20:00Z, world_yes: 0.44} [data, free].
   - Parallel reads within 4 s: Kalshi, Polymarket gamma + clob mids, HIP-4 outcomeMeta.
   - Returns fee-adjusted implied probabilities: World 44, Kalshi 46, Polymarket 45, HIP-4 43.
   - Lists resolution-rule differences: World uses Chainlink Data Streams, HIP-4 the mark price, and Brier the Chainlink ETH/USD aggregator on Base (last round at or before expiry).
3) The agent calls brier_quote {spec, buyer: 0xU} [data].
   - Fee $1.00; refund rule r = min(1, 4(p - outcome)^2); bond health (collateral $50, $6 locked); quote_id.
   - The plugin reads eth_getCode(0xU). If the wallet is EIP-7702-delegated, it warns that PayBox will undelegate first, because x402 needs a plain EOA.
4) The agent calls brier_buy [x402 proposal]: POST https://api.brier.markets/v1/forecasts {quote_id, buyer}, eip155:8453, maxAmount 1000000, 4-min expiry. The live 402's payTo is the forecaster's payout wallet. APPROVAL 1/1: passkey. PayBox signs EIP-3009.
5) Contract-as-facilitator: the backend submits BrierBond.sell(auth, sale). In one transaction, the bond:
   - calls USDC.transferWithAuthorization, so the fee goes straight to the forecaster;
   - records {buyer, fee, commitment = keccak(p, salt), feed, strike, expiry, market price m};
   - locks $1 of the forecaster's own collateral, reverting if collateral can't cover the maximum refund (then nothing settles and the user is never charged).
   The backend returns {p: 0.63, salt, rationale, sale_id, tx}.
6) The agent passes the paid response to brier_reveal [data].
   - The plugin verifies that the same tx contains both the USDC Transfer and SaleRegistered, that keccak(p, salt) matches the on-chain commitment, that collateral is locked, and that USDC.authorizationState(buyer, nonce) shows the authorization used.
   - 'Sealed before the outcome: 63% YES vs market 44%. If YES you get 55c back; if NO, the full $1.'
   - Adds a Kelly-capped size and a ready use_plugin handoff for World 'buy YES'. That is an optional second approval through the geofenced first-party World plugin; Brier itself never trades.
7) At 20:00Z the keeper (or anyone) calls BrierBond.settle(sale_id, p, salt, roundId).
   - The contract proves roundId is the last Chainlink round at or before expiry, computes the outcome and r, and pays r x fee from collateral to 0xU.
   - It updates the on-chain record: n, sum of Brier scores, and sum of the market's Brier scores.
   - Fallbacks: if the keeper fails, brier_settle returns the same call as an evm proposal. If the forecast is never revealed, the full fee is refunded after a 24 h grace period.
8) brier_status and brier_record [data] show the refund tx and the forecaster's verifiable skill versus the market.
   VISIBLE OUTCOME: a refund lands with zero taps, plus a tamper-proof public track record.
concepts.wow_moment: At 20:00 UTC the outcome lands. With nobody tapping anything, the forecaster's own collateral pays the user exactly min(1, 4(p - outcome)^2) of the fee on Basescan: the full $1 if the call was wrong, 55c if it was right at 63%. The forecast had been committed in the same transaction as the payment, hours earlier, so it could not have been edited after the fact.
concepts.novel_mechanism:
Information priced by a proper scoring rule and guaranteed by collateral.
- The refund is fee x min(1, 4(p - o)^2). An uninformative 50% call is free, a confident correct call keeps nearly the whole fee, and a confident wrong call is fully refunded.
- Because the Brier score is proper, the forecaster maximizes expected revenue only by reporting what it truly believes.
- 'Contract-as-facilitator' x402 settlement makes payment and forecast commitment atomic: the bond contract itself submits the buyer's EIP-3009 authorization and records the sale.
- Every guarantee is fully collateralized at sale time, with the on-chain invariant locked <= collateral.
- Settlement is trustless via a Chainlink round-bracket proof on Base, and the track record is tamper-proof.
- Buyer funds never sit in any contract: the fee goes straight to the seller, and refunds come from the seller's own money.

concepts.backend_and_contracts:
CONTRACT: BrierBond on Base (Foundry, verified, immutable).
- deposit / withdrawFree: only unlocked collateral can be withdrawn.
- sell(TransferWithAuthorization auth, Sale s): operator-only. Calls USDC.transferWithAuthorization; requires auth.from == s.buyer and auth.value == s.fee; locks s.fee; reverts if locked + fee > collateral.
- settle(saleId, p, salt, roundId): anyone. Checks the commitment, proves the Chainlink AggregatorV3 round brackets expiry (updatedAt(round) <= expiry < updatedAt(round+1)), pays refund = fee x min(1, 4(p-o)^2) in fixed point, unlocks, and updates stats including the market's Brier score.
- expireUnrevealed(saleId): anyone, after expiry + 24 h; full refund.
- Per-sale cap $5. v1 scope is Chainlink-settled crypto price thresholds (ETH, BTC, SOL).

BACKEND: Hono on Cloudflare Workers.
- Consensus aggregator.
- Forecasting engine: risk-neutral digital pricing N(d2) from Deribit/Hyperliquid volatility, a venue ensemble, and an LLM news sanity pass using the builder's Planner/Critic pattern from Ripcord.
- Quote store with a deterministic quote_id, so the approval-time 402 re-fetch is identical.
- x402 v2 resource server that self-facilitates through BrierBond.sell.
- Cron keeper that finds the bracketing roundId and settles.
- Public calibration page that reads only from chain.

concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability:
The buyer's fee goes from the builder's PayBox wallet directly to the forecaster payout wallet, which is also the builder's. Refunds flow from BrierBond collateral (the builder's own ~$50, withdrawable once sales settle) back to the buyer (the builder).
- Every dollar stays in builder-controlled wallets.
- Irreversible costs: gas for sell and settle (about $0.01 each on Base) and the bond deployment (about $0.50).
- The optional World 'enter' leg is the only non-recoverable spend; it can be skipped or done with $1.
- Total at risk is under $10.
concepts.compliance:
- Information product, not a wager. The buyer can never receive more than they paid (refund <= fee), and the payout is a function of forecast error (accuracy pricing), not of the event alone.
- No trading, no order routing, no positions. The 'enter' leg is handed to PayBox's own geofenced World plugin, so PayBox enforces eligibility.
- Non-custodial: buyer funds never sit in a contract, and the collateral is the seller's own money.
- No credentials: no venue API keys, public data only, and brokered headers for the builder's own backend and RPC.
- v1 is limited to crypto-price thresholds settled by Chainlink (no sports, no elections), with a $5 per-sale cap and 'not financial advice' plus resolution-basis disclosures.
- How regulators would classify outcome-contingent refunds is flagged for legal review before public listing.
concepts.differentiation:
- World (first-party) is the venue. Brier is the price-and-settle layer and hands entry to World instead of duplicating it. Hyperliquid's first-party plugin is read-only.
- The curated x402 set sells raw data and prices (Birdeye, Arkham, Blocksize); none sells forecasts, let alone guaranteed ones.
- MoonPay's moonpay-scout and prediction-market skills are arb scanners and trading wrappers with stale fee math.
- predictionmarketspicks-style x402 tools charge whether right or wrong, and tipsters and signal sellers have unverifiable records.
- ForecastBench measures forecasters but sells nothing.
- Nobody combines an atomic x402 commitment, collateralized refunds and a proper scoring rule.
key_risks: Outcome-contingent refunds could be read as event contracts/swaps by a compliance-minded judge
Forecast quality: a mis-calibrated model bleeds collateral
The demo outcome is random (right vs wrong cannot be scripted)
PayBox x402 interop with a self-facilitating server whose settlement tx is a contract call (PAYMENT-RESPONSE points at BrierBond.sell)
Chainlink heartbeat/deviation lag at expiry, and basis vs World's Data Streams
Keeper downtime delaying refunds
Thin product-market fit if World volume inside PayBox is small
concepts.mitigations:
- Frame and enforce it as accuracy pricing: refund <= fee, no leverage, no positions. Keep v1 to Chainlink-settled crypto thresholds, route all 'enter' through PayBox's geofenced World plugin, and publish a one-page legal rationale.
- The fully collateralized invariant and the per-sale cap bound losses. Quotes are withheld when the model's edge over the market is below a threshold.
- Both branches make a good demo (partial vs full refund), so film whichever outcome happens.
- Test the self-facilitated settlement against PayBox on day 1 with a $0.10 fee. Fall back to plain settlement plus a separate register() call if needed; brier_reveal can verify either.
- Disclose the resolution basis in brier_consensus.
- Buyer-side brier_settle fallback plus the 24 h full-refund expiry.
- The free consensus tool is useful on its own and feeds the paid funnel.
- The scoring design and model are the builder's own, documented in the repo.

concepts.name: Up NEPA
concepts.one_liner: Keep the lights on back home: buy a prepaid electricity token for any Nigerian meter from your AI chat. The plugin confirms the name on the meter, you approve one USDC payment, and you are charged only if the 20-digit token is actually issued.
concepts.target_user: Nigerian diaspora and Nigeria-based USDC holders who pay family utility bills (prepaid meters run out every week or two), plus any PayBox user running a household abroad. Founder-market fit if the builder has his own Nigerian corridor. The same backend can later add other STS prepaid-meter markets (Ghana, Kenya, South Africa) with no plugin change.
concepts.problem: Paying a relative's prepaid electricity from abroad today means off-ramping first. PayBox has get_buy_link but no off-ramp, and MoonPay sell and Paycrest need partner keys or KYB. Then comes a Nigerian bank app or a relative with cash. Tokens are meter-bound and irreversible, so one wrong digit is money gone. DisCos silently deduct arrears from purchases, and vends sometimes hang 'pending' after you have paid. No first-party plugin, core tool or curated x402 service vends utilities. The gift-card-style x402 commerce that exists (Bitrefill: search, detail, invoice, pay) takes several approvals and never verifies the recipient.
concepts.hero_flow: Host: Claude.ai with the PayBox connector; Up NEPA enabled under Unofficial plugins. 1) User: 'Mum's light is about to finish. Buy ₦10,000 of Ikeja Electric for meter 45001234567.' 2) Agent: discover_plugins → use_plugin(upnepa.verify_meter, {country:'NG', provider_id:'ikeja-electric', meter_number, meter_type:'prepaid'}) [data]. The backend calls VTpass POST /api/merchant-verify. Result: 'ADEBAYO F*** · Ikeja · PREPAID · Can_Vend true · arrears ₦0'. Agent: 'Is this Mum?' User: yes. 3) Agent: core get_portfolio (USDC on Base ≥ 7.6, plain EOA) → use_plugin(upnepa.quote_power, {meter_ref, amount_local:10000, rail:'base', payer:'0x…'}) [data]. Result: quote_id, 7.51 USDC (Paycrest public rate ~₦1,352/USDC + disclosed 1.5% fee), valid 240 s, payer screened via GoPlus. If short, needs_funding with the exact shortfall: the agent calls core get_buy_link (usdc_base) or request_swap, or withdraws from first-party jupiter Earn and pays on the Solana rail. 4) Agent: use_plugin(upnepa.buy_power, {quote_id}, wallet_id) → x402 proposal {chain eip155:8453, asset USDC 0x8335…2913, maxAmount 7510000, POST https://api.upnepa.app/v1/vend {quote_id}, expiresAt +4 min}, with the summary '7.51 USDC → Up NEPA for a ₦10,000 IKEDC token to ADEBAYO F*** (meter ••4567). Charged only if the token is issued.' 5) PayBox fetches the live 402 (side-effect free: payTo = merchant wallet, 7.51 USDC, maxTimeoutSeconds 300), checks asset and amount, and opens the transaction window. APPROVAL 1 (passkey/Face ID). 6) PayBox signs EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization and re-POSTs with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. The backend runs the x402 v2 'authorization' flow: facilitator /verify → re-screen 'from' → VTpass POST /api/pay (request_id derived from payer+nonce) → code 000 / status delivered → facilitator /settle → 200 {order_id, token, units, EIP-712 receipt} + PAYMENT-RESPONSE tx hash. If the vend fails: no settle, no charge. If pending: VTpass re-query, and settlement only on delivery before validBefore. 7) Agent: core get_request until terminal → use_plugin(upnepa.get_token, {order_id, paid_response}) [data]. Verifies the Base USDC Transfer (payer→merchant, 7.51) and the receipt signature. Returns '#### #### #### #### #### · N kWh · settled 2 s after issue' plus WhatsApp share text. 8) Visible outcome: Mum keys the token into the meter, it beeps 'Accept', and the lights come on.
concepts.wow_moment: Face ID abroad, and four seconds later 20 digits appear in Claude. Cut to Lagos: Mum keys them into the meter, it beeps 'Accept', the fan spins up and the room yells 'UP NEPA!' (what Nigerians shout when power returns). The Base settlement tx is stamped seconds AFTER the token was issued.
concepts.novel_mechanism: Delivery-versus-payment over x402 for an irreversible real-world good. The vend endpoint uses x402 v2's default 'authorization' flow: verify the EIP-3009 authorization, vend via VTpass, settle only on 'delivered'. The payer's signature therefore behaves like a check cashed only if a token exists. Pending vends are re-queried and settled only on delivery before validBefore; otherwise the authorization simply expires uncharged. Three more pieces: (1) the x402 payment nonce is the vend idempotency key, so retries cannot double-vend; (2) a bank-style 'name enquiry' on the meter (masked holder, arrears, Can_Vend) happens before the approval, not after the loss; (3) an EIP-712 merchant receipt binds token-hash, meter-hash and the USDC tx, so get_token can prove exactly what was bought.

concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability: User USDC (Base or Solana) moves by EIP-3009 straight to the builder's merchant wallet, settled only after VTpass reports 'delivered'; the facilitator pays settle gas. The builder's pre-funded VTpass NGN float pays the DisCo. In the demo the builder is both buyer and merchant, so every USDC lands back in his own merchant wallet. The only irreversible spend is the electricity itself, a real purchase his family uses (about ₦10,000-20,000, roughly $7.5-15 at Paycrest's ~₦1,352/USDC), plus cents of gas. Float top-up is about ₦20,000 (~$15); total demo budget under $30. Failed vends cost nothing because they are never settled.
concepts.compliance: No custody: payer pays merchant directly via EIP-3009, settled only on delivery, and no user balances are held. The builder is merchant of record for a digital good (prepaid electricity tokens) bought through a Nigerian VAS aggregator (VTpass). There is no cash-out and no P2P transfer, so it is bill pay, not a remittance or money-transmission service. Geo-scoped by design: vends only to Nigerian DisCo meters, and tool descriptions state availability (the plugin cannot see user location). The payer address is screened with GoPlus (sanctions/phishing) at quote and again at payment. Per-order cap (e.g., ₦50,000) and per-payer daily cap. FX is transparent: rate source and fee are shown before approval, and settlement is refused if the rate moved past the buffer. PII is minimised: holder name and address are masked in tool output, meter numbers are hashed in logs, and the merchant phone fills VTpass's phone field, so no customer phone is collected. Credentials: VTpass keys live only on the backend; plugin to backend auth is a brokered header; no user credentials anywhere. Disclosures: tokens are final once issued, and arrears deductions are shown up front. Must respect VTpass reseller terms.
concepts.differentiation: First-party plugins (world, aave, kamino, jupiter, hyperliquid, sunrise) are all DeFi or trading; none touch real-world bills. Core: get_buy_link is on-ramp only; request_transfer cannot pay a DisCo; request_payment cards are USD-only and DisCo checkouts need a browser. Curated x402 commerce is Bitrefill (gift cards/top-ups, multi-step, several approvals, no recipient verification), laso (a US prepaid card), AgentRes/Resy and BRIJ flights. Launch partners (AgentRes, Purch/Amazon, BRIJ) are US-centric consumer commerce. Off-ramps (MoonPay sell, Paycrest) need partner keys or KYB and deliver cash, not the bill. In a field of US-centric yield bots, data wrappers and Amazon clones, almost nobody will ship an Africa-first essential-utility rail with pay-on-delivery semantics, and nobody else's demo ends with a room lighting up.
key_risks: VTpass live API onboarding (KYC/verification) and NGN float funding may take days; no live vend means a failed gate
PayBox's paid re-fetch timeout and its handling of late settlement for pending vends are undocumented
x402 v2 interop between PayBox plugin proposals and a self-built resource server must be proven on mainnet
Judges outside Nigeria cannot test a vend without a meter number
Could be pattern-matched to the 'another prepaid/gift-card plugin' kill-list item
A token can be vended but settlement then fail (payer drained funds between verify and settle), leaving the builder out of pocket

Handling third-party PII (meter-holder name and address)

concepts.mitigations: Start VTpass live onboarding and float funding immediately. Keep the backend aggregator-agnostic so a second Nigerian VAS provider can be swapped in after the upload lock: hosts, variables and secrets stay editable, and tool schemas use generic provider_id/meter_number/amount_local fields. Prove interop on day 1 with a ₦1,000 mainnet vend on both rails. Keep the paid handler fast (verify ~1 s, vend in seconds, settle immediately). Re-query pending vends for up to ~6 s, then return a pending status and settle only on delivery before validBefore, so nobody is ever charged without a token. Re-check payer balance and screening just before vending to cap unpaid-vend loss. Give judges a designated demo meter (the builder's family home) and documented inputs so they can complete a real vend for under $1. Lead every surface with meter verification and pay-on-delivery so it reads as bill pay, not a gift card. Show arrears and FX before approval and refuse settlement on excessive rate drift. Detect delegation (eth_getCode 0xef0100 prefix) and route to PayBox's undelegate flow or the Solana rail. Mask PII and never log raw names, addresses or meter numbers.

concepts.name: orElse
concepts.one_liner: promise.orElse(): stake USDC on a promise to yourself. One x402 approval locks it at an escrow address that is literally the hash of your terms. Keep your word and you collect it back; break it and it goes where you said it would.
concepts.target_user: Builders, students, creators and anyone who already uses Claude or ChatGPT as a coach and wants real stakes on a habit: shipping code daily, saving weekly, staying off memecoins. They should not have to hand a card or funds to a custodial platform. Engineer-judges are the archetypal user.
concepts.problem: Agents can remind you, but they cannot make quitting cost anything. Commitment devices work because money is at stake, yet existing ones are custodial (card on file, pooled pots), and nothing in PayBox can hold your own stake neutrally. x402 itself has no escrow or refund path: the auth-capture scheme has no public facilitator support and the refund extension (PR #3681) is unmerged. So 'pay now, get it back if…' is impossible with a normal x402 payment, and AuthCaptureEscrow-based designs need approve + preApprove (two approvals) or relayed typed data.
concepts.hero_flow: Host: Claude.ai + PayBox; orElse enabled. 1) User: 'Pledge $20 that I push to github.com/demilade/ripcord every day until Friday. If I miss a day, send it to my brother 0xB0….' 2) Agent: use_plugin(orelse.draft_pledge, {goal_kind:'github_daily_push', goal_params:{repo, tz:'Africa/Lagos'}, stake_usdc:'20', deadline, fail_to:'0xB0…', payer:'0x…'}) [data]. Returns canonical terms, termsHash, escrow 0x7f3a… = CREATE2(PledgeFactory, keccak256(terms)) computed locally, proof tag 'orelse:7f3a', and the plain-English contract: 'kept → $20 back to you; missed → $20 to 0xB0…; oracle silent past deadline+72h → anyone can refund you'. 3) Agent: core get_portfolio (≥20 USDC on Base, plain EOA) → use_plugin(orelse.make_pledge, {terms}, wallet_id) → x402 proposal {chain eip155:8453, USDC, maxAmount 20000000, POST https://api.orelse.app/v1/pledges {terms}, expiry 4 min}. 4) PayBox fetches the 402. payTo is the predicted escrow address, derived deterministically from the POST body (no side effects). PayBox opens the window. APPROVAL 1 (passkey = signing the pledge). PayBox signs EIP-3009 to the escrow address. The backend checks from == terms.payer, settles via the facilitator and indexes the pledge. Paid response: {pledge_id, escrow, settle_tx}. 5) Agent: get_request → use_plugin(orelse.pledge_status) [data] → Base: balanceOf(escrow) = 20 USDC, extcodesize 0 ('nothing deployed, nothing custodied'). Daily progress in chat, optionally via a PayBox Desktop automation. 6) Oracle cron reads GitHub commits (proof tag in the first commit, non-empty diffs, per-day windows) and stores sha256'd evidence. At the deadline it signs an EIP-712 Verdict{termsHash, kept:true, evidenceHash}. 7) User: 'Collect my pledge.' → use_plugin(orelse.settle_pledge) → EVM proposal {chain eip155:8453, to PledgeFactory, value 0, data resolve(terms, true, evidenceHash, sig)}. APPROVAL 2. PayBox simulates, signs, broadcasts and confirms; a clone is deployed at the escrow address and 20 USDC returns to the payer. 8) pledge_status verifies the Transfer and Resolved event. Failure path: a keeper calls resolve(kept:false) and $20 goes to the brother with no payer approval. Silent oracle: refund(terms). Variants on the same schema: 'Degen Detox' (no memecoin buys from this wallet, read from Base logs) and a savings streak verified against deposits made through first-party jupiter Earn or kamino.
concepts.wow_moment: BaseScan shows $20 sitting at an address with NO contract code. Voiceover: 'this address is my promise; my signature already committed to its terms'. Then a live git push flips the verdict and the money comes home. In the honestly staged failure, the builder's brother receives $20 on camera and loses it laughing.
concepts.novel_mechanism: Counterfactual escrow as x402 payTo. x402 'exact' (EIP-3009) commits the payer's signature to 'to'. Setting payTo = CREATE2(factory, keccak256(terms)) turns a plain one-approval x402 payment into a terms-bound escrow with refund semantics. It needs no auth-capture facilitator, no approve transaction and no custodian. Nothing is even deployed until resolution, and the clone that eventually appears can only pay the payer or the pre-committed recipient. The oracle is bounded: a binary EIP-712 verdict carrying an evidence hash, so it can never choose a third destination. Liveness favours the user: permissionless refund after deadline + grace. An optional outcome-independent fee means the operator never profits from your failure. Product-wise it inverts the Predictions track: 'price, enter, settle' on yourself, with no venue, counterparty, geofence or EIP-712.

concepts.backend_and_contracts: Base contracts (Foundry; verified, immutable, no admin, ~150 LOC). PledgeFactory exposes predict(terms), resolve(terms, kept, evidenceHash, sig) and refund(terms), with EIP-712 verdict verification and replay protection keyed by termsHash. PledgeEscrow is an EIP-1167 clone deployed via CREATE2 with salt = keccak256(abi.encode(terms)) only at resolution; its single release(to) is callable only by the factory, and the factory enforces to ∈ {payer, failTo}. Also GET /v1/pledges/{id}, POST /v1/pledges/{id}/check and GET /v1/verdicts/{id}. The oracle is a Workers Cron job reading the GitHub REST API (server token, ETags) and Base logs via Alchemy; Solana reads for savings-streak goals use the public Kamino/Jupiter position APIs. Evidence JSON goes to R2 with its sha256 in the verdict. A keeper wallet executes forfeits and stale refunds (gas: cents). Factory and oracle addresses are plugin env vars, editable after the upload lock, so the bundle ships before contracts are final.

concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability: Payer USDC goes to a counterfactual escrow address, one per pledge with nothing pooled. It returns to the payer on success or after an oracle-silence timeout, or goes to the payer-chosen recipient on failure. Demo money is 100% recoverable except the intentionally staged forfeit ($5-20 to the builder's brother, so it stays in the family). Gas: the facilitator pays settlement; resolve/refund costs cents on Base (payer on collect, keeper on forfeits). Budget: ~$40 cycled through pledges, under $1 gas, contract deployment at cents.
concepts.compliance: Not gambling: no counterparty stakes, no chance element, and the payer can never receive more than their own stake. That is the established commitment-contract structure, and product copy says 'pledge', never 'bet' or 'odds'. Non-custodial: no admin keys, no upgradeability, no pooled balances; each escrow can only pay the payer or the pre-committed recipient, and if the oracle disappears anyone can refund the payer after grace. The oracle is bounded and auditable (signed verdict + public evidence hash). No credential pass-through: GitHub goals use public data plus an in-commit proof tag (no OAuth tokens through the agent), and on-chain goals use the payer address itself. Recipients default to a verified charity list; friend recipients are GoPlus-screened, warned and disabled where local rules require. Per-pledge cap, 18+, and an outcome-independent fee only. No geofenced venue is touched, and tool descriptions state eligibility.
concepts.differentiation: First-party world is counterparty event markets (geofenced, MCP-only); orElse has no market, no counterparty and nothing to geofence. Kalshi/Polymarket trading is on the kill list, and orElse touches no venue. Core approvals and grants restrict spending but cannot make quitting costly. Curated x402 services offer no escrow or refunds (auth-capture is unsupported by facilitators). Escrow entries built on AuthCaptureEscrow (0xf968…B19c) need approve + preApprove or agent-signed typed data relayed by the plugin, which reviewers may read as bypassing plugin approval; orElse needs one plain x402 approval. Off-platform commitment apps keep a card on file (custodial), and habit-staking dApps pool everyone's money in one contract. orElse is per-pledge, admin-less and self-refundable.
key_risks: A bug in the factory or clone could lock or misroute escrowed USDC
A facilitator or PayBox could reject or flag a per-request dynamic payTo
Oracle trust and goal gaming (empty commits, someone else's repo)
A compliance-minded panel could read it as gambling
Week-long goals are hard to show in 90 seconds
GitHub API limits or outages delaying verdicts
x402 requires a plain-EOA payer (7702-delegated wallets fail)
concepts.mitigations: Minimal immutable contracts with Foundry fuzz and invariant tests ('funds only ever reach payer or failTo'; 'refund always possible after grace'), a per-pledge cap and $1 mainnet dry runs. Test dynamic payTo on day 1 with both PayAI and CDP; fallback is self-facilitation (the backend submits transferWithAuthorization, still payer-signed to the predicted address). Make goals hard to fake: proof tag in the first commit, non-empty diffs, per-day windows, evidence hash inside the verdict. Cheating only cheats yourself because there is no counterparty. 'Pledge' copy, charity-default recipients, outcome-independent fee only, no upside for the payer. A server-side GitHub token with ETag caching avoids rate limits. The demo shows a real 3-minute micro-pledge on camera, plus an honestly labelled time-lapse of a week-long pledge and a staged forfeit. Check eth_getCode for 7702 delegation before proposing x402.

concepts.name: Proof of Life
concepts.one_liner: A will for your agent wallet. One approval gives a capped USDC allowance to an address that encodes your heirs. Every passkey check-in is proof of life, and only prolonged silence lets your family inherit; your money never leaves your wallet until then.
concepts.target_user: PayBox users holding meaningful USDC in passkey/MPC wallets, which have no seed phrase to leave behind; crypto-native families; solo founders whose agents control business funds (key-person risk).
concepts.problem: PayBox wallets are MPC + passkey, so there is no paper seed phrase a family can find. Death or permanent incapacity strands the funds. Existing answers are exchange estate desks (custodial), smart-account recovery modules that PayBox's MPC EOAs cannot use, or dead-man-switch vaults that make you move your money into someone's contract. As agents control more money, 'what happens to my agent's wallet when I'm gone?' has no answer in PayBox.
concepts.hero_flow: Host: Claude.ai + PayBox; Proof of Life enabled. 1) User: 'If I ever go silent for 90 days, send my Base USDC to my sister Ada (70%) and brother Tunde (30%).' 2) Agent: core get_portfolio (500 USDC on Base; optionally first-party aave plugin aave_position to include aBasUSDC) → use_plugin(pol.draft_will, {owner, chain:'eip155:8453', heirs:[{who:'ada.base.eth', bps:7000},{who:'0x7u…', bps:3000}], silence_days:90, grace_days:30, cap:'500'}) [data]. Resolves the Basename, GoPlus-screens the heirs, and computes W = CREATE2(HeirloomFactory, keccak256(terms)). Returns: 'Funds stay in your wallet. After 120 days with no check-in, W can pull up to 500 USDC: Ada 70%, Tunde 30%.' 3) Agent: use_plugin(pol.sign_will, {terms}, wallet_id) → EVM proposal {chain eip155:8453, to USDC 0x8335…2913, value 0, data approve(W, 500e6)}. APPROVAL 1 (passkey). 4) Agent: will_status [data] → allowance(owner, W) = 500, W has no code, next deadline date. Optionally registers termsHash and deadline (not heirs) for reminders, and hands over letter_to_heirs. 5) Later: user says 'I'm alive' (or a PayBox Desktop reminder fires) → use_plugin(pol.check_in, {terms}) → EVM proposal {to HeirloomFactory, data checkIn(terms)}. APPROVAL 2 (Face ID = proof of life); a CheckedIn event resets the clock. 6) After 90+30 days of silence, a keeper, or an heir via execute_will (EVM proposal from the heir's own PayBox), calls execute(terms). A clone is deployed at W and pulls min(allowance, balance) from the owner to Ada and Tunde by bps. 7) The demo runs step 6 live with a clearly labelled demo-mode will (2-minute silence, 1-minute grace, 25 USDC cap, separate demo factory): Ada receives 17.50 USDC and Tunde 7.50 on BaseScan.
concepts.wow_moment: The builder does nothing, and that is the trigger. Two minutes after his last Face ID his sister's phone buzzes with USDC pulled straight from his PayBox wallet by the address that is his will. She calls: 'Demi?? Did you just die?' He answers: 'Only in the demo.'
concepts.novel_mechanism: Allowance-as-a-will plus approvals-as-heartbeat. A single ERC-20 approve to W = CREATE2(factory, keccak256(heirs, shares, silence, grace, start, salt)) is the entire will. Funds never leave the wallet, no contract exists until execution, and the only code that can ever appear at W pays the committed heirs, after the committed silence, up to the cap. Each check-in is a PayBox passkey-approved transaction, so proof of life is literally biometric, and the absence of approvals is the trigger. That turns PayBox's approval model from friction into the product. Execution is permissionless, so no backend is needed for correctness. A deterministic-deployer factory gives the same contract address on every eip155 chain PayBox supports.

The companion API is optional for correctness: escalating reminders (owner at T-14d and T, heirs at T+grace/2 if opted in), an opt-in keeper (stores terms to auto-execute at maturity; gas cents), and a status indexer. concepts.money_flow_and_recoverability: Nothing moves at setup: approve(W, cap) only grants an allowance, and check-ins cost Base gas (cents). On execution USDC moves straight from owner to heirs. In the demo the heirs are the builder's siblings, so the 25 USDC stays in the family and can be sent back. Revocation is approve(W, 0). Budget: ~$25 demo inheritance + ~$1 gas + cents of deployment, fully recoverable.
concepts.compliance: Non-custodial by construction: funds stay in the owner's PayBox wallet; the only on-chain right is a capped allowance usable only after the committed silence and only to the committed heirs; no admin, no upgrades. Not a legal will: explicit disclaimer, plus a letter_to_heirs with on-chain proof for executors; jurisdiction-specific estate law (e.g., forced heirship) is flagged. Safety rails: production minimum silence ≥30 days and grace ≥14 days, escalating reminders, any check-in cancels, heirs GoPlus-screened, capped allowances only (no unlimited approvals). Privacy: private mode keeps heirs off-chain until execution and off the backend entirely; keeper mode is opt-in. No credentials of any kind, only public addresses and on-chain calls. Geo-agnostic.
concepts.differentiation: No first-party plugin (world, aave, kamino, jupiter, hyperliquid, sunrise) and no core tool handles inheritance or recovery; curated x402 services and launch partners are irrelevant to it. Exchange estate desks are custodial. Multisig inheritance services rely on a coordinating company. Safe recovery modules need a Safe smart account, which PayBox's MPC EOAs are not. Dead-man-switch vaults require depositing funds into the vault. Proof of Life keeps funds in the PayBox wallet, uses PayBox's own passkey as the heartbeat and needs one approval to set up. Few hackathon entrants will design for death, and judges will remember the one that did.

concepts.mitigations: Tiny immutable contracts with invariant tests (only heirs, only after silence, only up to the allowance) and capped allowances, seeded with small amounts first and verified source. Production minimums plus escalating reminders (agent chat, PayBox Desktop automation, email); any check-in cancels, and a false positive pays family, not strangers. A clear 'not a legal will' disclaimer and an executor-ready letter with on-chain proof. A separate, clearly labelled demo-mode factory with short minimums, while the production 90-day setting is shown first. Private mode stores no heirs off-chain; an heir needs only an address (a fresh MoonPay/PayBox wallet works). will_status re-checks coverage, and the agent prompts a re-sign when balances move. concepts.why_it_wins_first: It is the entry the PayBox team will wish they had built. It fixes a structural gap of passkey/MPC wallets (nothing to inherit) by using PayBox's own approval model as the mechanism: each Face ID is a heartbeat, and silence is the trigger. Setup is one approval with zero custody on minimal code. The demo carries a real gasp and a real laugh, and the outcome is a real person receiving real USDC. No third-party API sits in the critical path, which makes it the most robust live test a judge can run. It scores on usefulness (a universal, unsolved need sharpened by PayBox's design), PayBox-native depth (approvals as the product), a non-cliché mechanism (allowance-as-will to a counterfactual address) and a memorable demo.
